item.title: Energy, Passivity, and Diffusive Representations in Anisotropic Fractional Maxwell--Cole--Cole Media
item.description: arXiv:2610.13985v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study develops an energy formulation for linear anisotropic Maxwell--Cole--Cole media with multiple fractional polarization channels, passive conductivity, prescribed currents, and finite-terminal Caputo memory with zero prehistory. A weighted solution class captures the integrable fractional initial layer generated by quiescent polarization. Fractional polarization power then separates into a nonnegative history storage and a nonnegative constitutive dissipation rate. Although the instantaneous rate may diverge at initialization, it remains integrable, while stored history energy and accumulated loss vanish initially. Combined with the Poynting theorem, this decomposition yields a global field-plus-memory identity that establishes electromagnetic passivity, closed-system energy decay, and conditional uniqueness under zero-supply boundary conditions. The framework also recovers the Debye, instantaneous-dielectric, vanishing-susceptibility, and vacuum limits under convergence assumptions. A positive diffusive representation provides a second decomposition whose storage never exceeds the history storage. Their difference is an exact nonnegative weighted variance that vanishes only for a zero polarization history. In agreement with these time-domain results, the finite-time harmonic response approaches the anisotropic multichannel Cole--Cole permittivity, whose Hermitian imaginary part ensures nonnegative cycle-averaged absorption. A reproducible single-channel study shows that fractional order broadens the dielectric-loss band, redistributes wave attenuation, strengthens the integrable initial power layer, and prolongs the step-response tail. An exact electric-step response verifies both energy representations. The formulation connects fractional initial layers, hereditary storage, passivity, diffusive relaxation, dispersion, absorption, and attenuation in a local constitutive model.
item.dc:creator: Nikko John Leo S. Lobos

item.title: Comment on "Landau Levels and Riemann Zeros"
item.description: arXiv:2610.14108v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sierra and Townsend (ST) [1] showed that the ``absorption spectrum'' model of Connes [2] arises as the lowest-Landau-level (LLL) limit of a charged particle in crossed electric and magnetic fields, and suggested that the higher Landau levels supply the fluctuation part of the Riemann-zero counting function $N(E)$. Within the approximation used by ST we construct the eigenfunctions of an arbitrary Landau level $n$ and derive their asymptotics at the two box boundaries that ST identify. The boundary condition is the same as for $n=0$ up to an $E$-independent phase $(-\ii)^n$, so no $\ln E$ term arises for any fixed $n$. We also note that the $\ln E$ term in the semiclassical Eq.~(29) of ST is the first-order shift of the smooth LLL counting function, $E\to E+\gamma z^2$.
item.dc:creator: Mi-Ra Hwang, Eylee Jung, MuSeong Kim, DaeKil Park

item.title: Categorifying Quantum Spin Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.14165v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a homotopical framework for understanding the space of quantum spin systems based on topological $n$-nets, which assign associative unital algebras to local regions in an $n$-dimensional space in a manner that captures the locality structure of the underlying lattice theories. The net-theoretic perspective admits a natural categorification, in which the category of topological $n$-nets carries the structure of a higher Morita category. Moreover, the nets of greatest physical interest form a Karoubi-complete subcategory that shares many of the characteristic structural features of the category of finite TQFTs. Our main result identifies the group of locality-preserving symmetries of (3+1)-dimensional quantum spin systems (i.e. quantum cellular automata modulo stabilization, finite-depth quantum circuits, and translations) with the full Witt group of nondegenerate braided fusion categories, thereby answering a question posed by Haah.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Yu

item.title: An Introduction to the $p$-Differential Forms in Spinor Variables on the Minkowskian Manifold
item.description: arXiv:2610.14240v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article presents an introductory study of $p$-differential forms in spinor variables defined on the Minkowskian (or Lorentzian) manifold. Starting from the algebraic and geometric foundations of spinor spaces and Clifford algebras, we establish the correspondence between Minkowski spacetime and Hermitian matrices in spinor coordinates. Within this framework, we construct differential 1-forms and 2-forms expressed in spinor notation, and formulate the Dirac operator in terms of exterior calculus. Furthermore, we extend this approach to the case of non-monogenic functions, following the method proposed in~\cite{Jaramillo2024}. The results illustrate the consistency of the spinorial exterior calculus and its potential applications in the study of relativistic field equations and geometric formulations of quantum theory.
item.dc:creator: Julio C\'esar Jaramillo Quiceno

item.title: Inverse Resonance Problem for the Half-Line Schr\"odinger Operator with a Complex Robin Boundary Condition
item.description: arXiv:2610.14323v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the inverse resonance problem for the one-dimensional Schr\"odinger operator on the half-line with a compactly supported complex-valued potential and a complex Robin boundary condition \[ u'(0)-a u(0)=0,\qquad a\in\mathbb C. \] The proof follows the transformation-operator, entire-function, and Fourier analytic strategy developed by Marletta, Shterenberg and Weikard for the Dirichlet problem \cite{MSW}. The Dirichlet Jost function $\psi(z,0)$ is replaced by the Robin characteristic function \[ F_a(z;q)=\psi_x(z,0;q)-a\psi(z,0;q). \] We establish the corresponding large-energy estimates, Hadamard factorization, finite-data stability, and uniqueness results. The principal new feature is that $F_a(z;q)=iz-a+O(1)$ rather than $1+O(z^{-1})$. In the transformation-operator argument the relevant boundary quantity is $B_x(0,t)-aB(0,t)$, together with the scalar term $B(0,0)$. For fixed $a\in\mathbb C$, and uniformly for $a$ in bounded subsets of $\mathbb C$, the resulting inverse resonance estimates have the same qualitative form as those proved in \cite{MSW} for the Dirichlet problem. In particular, for a fixed Robin parameter $a$, the complete set of Robin eigenvalues and resonances, counted with multiplicity, determines the potential uniquely. The text is produced with the help of AI ChatGPT for Academy.
item.dc:creator: Roman Shterenberg

item.title: Yang-Mills Theory in the Multisymplectic Framework
item.description: arXiv:2610.14418v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This Master's thesis develops and applies the multisymplectic field-theory framework to (pure) Yang-Mills theory. Building from the geometric foundations of jet bundles and the Poincar\'e-Cartan forms, the work constructs the Lagrangian multisymplectic formalism for first-order field theories, recovering the usual Euler-Lagrange field equations and extending the Poisson brackets of symplectic mechanics to a full graded Lie algebra. It then establishes the Legendre correspondence with the multisymplectic Hamiltonian formalism (in which Hamilton equations are retrieved) including the case of singular Lagrangians (where a constraint algorithm is reproduced). Breaking Lorentz covariance via a Cauchy surface slicing, the thesis then relates the covariant multisymplectic picture to an instantaneous presymplectic (infinite-dimensional) formulation in which the instantaneous De Donder equations and presymplectic brackets are obtained in a compatible way. A comprehensive treatment of symmetries then leads to multisymplectic and instantaneous momentum maps generalizations and to several versions of Noether's theorems. Specializing the formalism to principal-bundle gauge theory, the thesis identifies the multisymplectic configuration space with the bundle of connections, gauge symmetries with symmetries in the multisymplectic language and builds the Yang-Mills Lagrangian. Lastly, among many computations, the standard tensorial Yang-Mills equations and the Bianchi identity in local trivializations are retrieved, Yang-Mills conserved currents and charges are obtained and the graded algebra is derived for a special class of Hamiltonian forms.
item.dc:creator: David Villa-Blanco

item.title: Non-Intrusive Balancing for Data-Driven Model Reduction with Oblique Projections
item.description: arXiv:2610.15219v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Non-intrusive reduced-order modeling is essential for systems simulated with black- or gray-box solvers, yet computing accurate data-driven models remains challenging when the dynamics exhibit large-amplitude transient energy growth. This is because state-of-the-art non-intrusive methods typically rely on orthogonal projection onto high-energy linear or nonlinear manifolds identified by minimizing static reconstruction losses, which truncates low-energy, yet dynamically important, states. Intrusive methods such as Balanced Truncation and its extensions address this issue by using adjoint information to define dynamics-aware oblique projections. Here, we show that balancing-based oblique projections for nonlinear systems can instead be computed non-intrusively from forward simulation data. Specifically, we develop a framework to compute the nonlinear empirical reachability Gramian and balance it against its observability counterpart, projected onto a suitable restriction subspace. This procedure provably recovers the oblique projection of Balanced Truncation when the dynamics are linear and the range of either Gramian is contained in the restriction subspace. Moreover, in the linear case and in the absence of adjoint information, we show that the minimax-optimal restriction subspace spans the dominant eigenspaces of the reachability Gramian, which informs an efficient balancing algorithm with cost comparable to a standard SVD. Once the oblique projection is computed, we use Operator Inference to learn the latent-space dynamics on its range. The method is demonstrated on several examples of increasing complexity, including the three-dimensional incompressible flow past a wing with $8\times 10^7$ degrees of freedom. In all examples, the Balanced Operator Inference models significantly outperform their POD-based counterparts, reducing forecasting error by up to two orders of magnitude.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Padovan

item.title: From isolated singular wells to exact Bloch bands: the trigonometric P\"oschl-Teller lattice
item.description: arXiv:2610.16072v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An exactly solvable lattice with periodic inverse-square singularities exhibits two physically distinct mechanisms of spectral-gap closure. The model arises from the generalized trigonometric P\"oschl-Teller potential in the coupling range where both local solutions at each singularity are square-integrable. A transmitting, current-preserving self-adjoint matching condition connects neighboring cells and generates a nontrivial Bloch spectrum. For a generic lattice with two inequivalent singular sublattices, the spectrum contains two alternating families of gaps, and the band edges reproduce the scale-invariant spectra of the associated finite singular system. One gap family closes when the two sublattices become equivalent. In this symmetric limit, however, the primitive period halves, so the apparent band crossing results from Brillouin-zone folding. A different family closes at a critical but genuinely asymmetric configuration. Because the primitive period is preserved, adjacent bands then meet at the center of the original Brillouin zone in a genuine massless Dirac-like cone. Near either critical limit, a small finite gap acts as an effective Dirac mass: the dispersion remains quadratic near a band edge but crosses over to a massive Dirac-like form beyond that narrow region. The band curvatures define effective electron and hole masses. Exact Bloch eigenfunctions further reveal that isospectral lattices can display different single-particle probability densities. This model therefore provides an analytically controlled one-dimensional setting in which conventional quadratic carriers, massive Dirac-like band dispersions, and a tunable massless contact coexist within the same singular lattice.
item.dc:creator: Ulysses Camara da Silva

item.title: The Fr\"ohlich Polaron at large total momentum in d=3
item.description: arXiv:2610.16081v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the three-dimensional Fr\"ohlich polaron at fixed coupling strength $\alpha>0$ and total momentum $P \in \bbR^3$. We show that the bottom of the spectrum reaches the essential spectrum at a finite value of $|P|$, implying that the fiber Hamiltonian has no ground state at sufficiently large total momentum. This extends the known weak-coupling result to arbitrary coupling. Our approach describes states near the spectral threshold by a fully interacting polaron with small residual momentum and one additional phonon carrying almost all of the total momentum.
item.dc:creator: Tobias Schmidt

item.title: Using the Renormalized Energy from Ginzburg-Landau Theory to Compute Solution Landscapes in the Reduced Landau-de Gennes Theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.16083v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study nematic liquid crystal phases confined to bounded, two-dimensional (2D) domains, in the reduced Landau-de Gennes (rLdG) theoretical framework. The rLdG framework is equivalent to the celebrated Ginzburg-Landau (GL) theoretical setting, under certain assumptions. In the asymptotic limit of large domains (or low temperatures), we recall the concept of the finite-dimensional renormalized energy in the GL theory [Bethuel et al., GL Vortices, Prog. Nonlinear Differ. Equ. Appl. 13, Birkh\"auser, 1994.] and generalize it to polygons with sharp corners. The renormalized energy is fully defined by the triplet, $(\mathbf{a},\mathbf{c}, \mathbf{d}$), of topological degrees of the interior defects ($\mathbf{d}$) and the winding number contribution of polygon vertices ($\mathbf{c}$) and interior defect locations ($\mathbf{a}$), subject to sum rules dictated by the imposed Dirichlet boundary condition. We use the critical points of the renormalized energy to construct initial conditions for the rLdG solver, recover known energy-minimizing and non-energy minimizing saddle points of the rLdG energy on a disc, regular hexagon and rectangle along with the discovery of previously unreported rLdG solution branches. The renormalized energy approach is computationally substantially more efficient than a direct PDE-solver in the rLdG setting but misses solution branches with line defects and finite-size effects.
item.dc:creator: Yucen Han, Apala Majumdar

item.title: Superintegrable systems in curved spaces via coalgebras and deformed Racah algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.16154v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the Poisson algebras generated by partial Casimirs of undeformed and non-standard $q$-deformed $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$ coalgebras, respectively. The derivation is performed on the abstract algebraic level and does not depend on any particular symplectic realization. For the 3- and 4-site cases the constructions associated with the undeformed $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$ produce the rank-one and rank-two Racah Poisson algebras, respectively, while those with the non-standard deformed $\mathfrak{sl}$ yield finite quadratic Poisson algebras generated by connected partial Casimirs. At both the three and four sites, the final closure coefficients do not explicitly depend on the deformation parameter. The results hold at the Poisson coalgebra level and hence apply to any realizations which preserve the defining brackets and coproducts. Canonical symplectic realizations give rise to Hamiltonians in spaces of non-constant curvature. For the St\"ackel $q$-deformed Smorodinsky-Winternitz model we show explicitly how the universal coalgebra sector is completed to maximal superintegrability. An exact two-block identity, proved directly in the localized Poisson algebra without appealing to a symplectic realization, controls the additional St\"ackel integrals. In three dimensions, it generates a quadratic Poisson block with its own Casimir relation; in four dimensions, its coupling to the full left/right coalgebra family is organized into three nested quadratic blocks, and the same identity extends this nested coupling to arbitrary $N$. Explicit higher-site partial Casimirs and factorized bracket generators are collected in the appendices.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Jimenez-Swain, Ian Marquette, Yao-Zhong Zhang

item.title: Geometric bulk conductances in even dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.16208v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $P$ be a short-range projector on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}^{2n},\mathbb{C}^m)$ and $U=(U_1,\dots,U_{2n})$ be a transverse family of open subsets of $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$. We give an elementary proof of a recent result of Martinian-Stoiber, which extends a two-dimensional result of Drouot-Zhu to all even dimensions. Specifically, using only Stokes' theorem and the Poincar\'e lemma, we show that the geometric Kubo formula $\operatorname{Tr}\big(P[P,\mathbf{1}_{U_1}]\wedge\cdots\wedge[P,\mathbf{1}_{U_{2n}}]\big)$ is the product of a topological integer $\mathcal{X}_U$, which depends only on the relative positions of $U_1, \dots, U_{2n}$, and of the bulk conductance of $P$. Our proof writes the geometric bulk conductance as the pairing of $P$ with a cochain on $\mathbb{Z}^{2n}$ - an idea originally due to Kitaev - and deforms the cochain rather than the sets $(U_1, \dots, U_{2n})$. The proof presented in this paper is due to Claude Opus 5.5.
item.dc:creator: Alexis Drouot

item.title: Nested polynomial algebras and the exact spectrum of a three-dimensional two-spin oscillator
item.description: arXiv:2610.16317v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct representations of the symmetry algebra and derive the exact spectrum of a three-dimensional oscillator with two spin-$\tfrac12$ degrees of freedom. The Hamiltonian and its first-order scalar and pseudo-scalar integrals were obtained in earlier classifications. Here we determine their action on the complete spectral basis. At fixed total angular momentum, a quadratic algebra acts on the three triplet orbital channels and admits a three-dimensional deformed-oscillator representation, while an overlapping two-state exchange algebra joins the middle triplet to the singlet. These finite modules determine angular--spin multiplicities but do not quantize the radial energy. A separate positive-discrete-series $su(1,1)$ representation of the common radial Hamiltonian generates the energy sequence. We give the finite matrices, Casimir and structure functions, normalized eigenfunctions, radial ladder actions, the exceptional $j=0$ sector, complete energy-shell multiplicities, and the effect of particle interchange.
item.dc:creator: Ian Marquette, O. Ogulcan Tuncer, I. Yurdusen

item.title: Almost invariant subspaces in the topologically non-trivial setting: a pedestrian approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.16393v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a self-contained, algorithmic construction of almost invariant subspaces [Panati et al. (2003), De Nittis and Panati (2010), Freund and Teufel (2016)] for Hofstadter-like Hamiltonians $H_b $ acting on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}^2,\mathbb{C}^n)$. More precisely, for rational values of $b_0/(2\pi)$ we describe an iterative procedure that takes a ``locally gapped" projection $P_{0}$ (possibly topologically non-trivial) which commutes with $H_{b_0}$, into a projection $P_{\varepsilon}$ that commutes with $H_{b_0+\varepsilon}$ up to an error of order $\varepsilon^\infty$. Our construction insures that the Chern number of $P_{\varepsilon}$ equals the Chern number of $P_0$ as long as $P_\varepsilon$ exists. Moreover, its integrated density of states varies linearly with $\varepsilon$ (the ``St\v{r}eda formula"). We also show that any spatially localized Parseval frame of $P_{0}$ can be mapped into to a localized Parseval frame of $P_{\varepsilon}$. We choose to work with a discrete model in order to keep the technicalities to a minimum level, with no need for advanced pseudo-differential calculus. Nevertheless, we are confident that most of our results can be extended to (unbounded) magnetic (pseudo)differential operators, but the technical burden would be much heavier. This is left for future work.
item.dc:creator: Horia Cornean, Gabriele Peluso, Mikkel Hviid Thorn

item.title: Willis-type thermal homogenization for particulate composites under harmonic heat transfer
item.description: arXiv:2610.17245v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops a Willis-type thermal homogenization framework for two-dimensional particulate composites under harmonic heat transfer and establishes a unique effective constitutive relation without introducing residual fields. The local thermal fields are obtained using the dual-reciprocity inclusion-based boundary element method, in which two eigen-fields are introduced to simulate the mismatches in thermal conductivity and heat capacity. Instead of retrieving effective kernels from several independent macroscopic solutions generated by residual fields, the complete constitutive operator is constructed upon relations between eigen-fields and generalized macroscopic responses. The effective constitutive relations are validated against a one-dimensional analytical solution and an extended Fourier-series homogenization scheme. The Fourier formulae further establish the opposite-wavenumber reciprocity relations between two coupling tensors and reflection-symmetry parity relations, which explain when transverse coupling components vanish and the sign reversal of off-diagonal conductivity components under reflection. Numerical results further demonstrate that the de-phased average is required to extract physically consistent effective thermal properties under the Bloch conditions, and reveal their nonlocal frequency/wavenumber-dependent behavior. The framework provides a general computational method for Willis-type homogenization of particulate composites and is extendable to three-dimensional, multiphysical problems.
item.dc:creator: Chunlin Wu, Ning Ding, Huiming Yin

item.title: Norm properties of quantum uniformity measures
item.description: arXiv:2610.17454v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that for $k=4$ the quantum uniformity measures are norms, whereas for every $k\geq5$ the triangle inequality fails. This gives a complete answer to an open question of Bu, Gu, and Jaffe. The $k=4$ case is proved using the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality for the quantum uniformity pairing $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{Q^4}$ introduced here, together with the triangle inequality in a suitable finite-dimensional Bochner $L^8$ space. For $k\geq5$, we construct systems of linear equations over a finite field and derive a contradiction from the structure theory of norming linear systems.
item.dc:creator: Berke \"Unal

item.title: $L^2$ convergence rates for singular stochastic wave dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.17815v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish quantitative hypocoercivity for singular stochastic damped wave equations arising in stochastic quantization. Building on the finite-dimensional argument of Cao, Lu, and Wang [Arch. Rat. Mech. Anal. 2023], we derive a dimension-free criterion that replaces uniform semiconvexity by a log-Sobolev inequality together with exponential lower-tail bounds for the bottom of the Hessian spectrum. We verify this criterion for the two-dimensional $\Phi^4_2$ and sine-Gordon models and for the three-dimensional $\Phi^4_3$ model, through estimates on the lowest eigenvalue of associated singular random Schr\"odinger operators. Combined with the continuum limit established in a companion paper, this yields exponential $L^2$ convergence to equilibrium for the $\Phi^4_2$ dynamics and for sine-Gordon with $\beta^2<2\pi$. For $\Phi^4_2$, we verify that in a weak-coupling, small-mass regime, optimizing the damping yields a kinetic relaxation rate of at least order $m$. This yields a genuine acceleration over the order-$m^2$ relaxation rate of the overdamped dynamics. The lattice estimates are uniform in the discretization for sine-Gordon throughout $\beta^2<4\pi$, and for $\Phi^4_3$ at fixed volume, including regimes beyond those for which the continuum dynamics is vpresently constructed.
item.dc:creator: Nikolay Barashkov, Giacomo Di Ges\`u, Petri Laarne

item.title: How many switches does two-Hamiltonian universality require?
item.description: arXiv:2610.17826v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Any pair of sufficiently generic Hamiltonians on $\mathbb{C}^d$ generates the full unitary group, i.e., any $W\in U(d)$ can be synthesized to arbitrary precision by alternating between the two evolutions for suitably chosen durations. For any given pair of Hamiltonians, the minimal number of switches required to cover the entire group is at least $d$ and unbounded in general. Despite this, we show that it scales linearly in $d$ in expectation. Assuming that the two spectra are sufficiently generic, we derive constructive upper bounds on the minimal switching number as a function of the change-of-basis matrix between the two eigenbases. In particular, if this matrix has a column whose entries all have equal moduli, as for a complex Hadamard matrix, then $9d$ switches suffice to reach every unitary. To obtain these results, we construct a short exact representation of any unitary as a product of unitaries that are alternately diagonal in two given bases. All bounds are extended to non-generic spectra and bounded evolution times.
item.dc:creator: Matas Garbaravi\v{c}ius, Michael M. Wolf

item.title: Dynamics of low energy wave packets in the one-dimensional quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet
item.description: arXiv:2610.17883v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spin wave theory plays a central role in the analysis of low-energy properties of the quantum ferromagnetic Heisenberg model. In this work, we present a first step towards a rigorous justification of this approximation in the context of quantum dynamics in one dimension. According to spin wave theory, the evolution of a spin wave state should be well approximated by its free evolution with the appropriate energy of free quasiparticles called magnons. Our main result establishes this idea rigorously for a class of spin wave packets. We focus on spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ systems, and consider wave packets composed of two magnons. We argue our result is optimal with respect to the timescales.
item.dc:creator: Mateusz Kwa\'snicki, Marcin Napi\'orkowski, S\"oren Petrat, Micha{\l} Pietruszka

item.title: Dynamical BEC formation and vanishing entropy for trapped bosons in non-relativistic QED via nonlinear resonance cascades
item.description: arXiv:2610.17923v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The dynamical formation of a complete Bose-Einstein condensate and the asymptotic purification of trapped bosons coupled to a quantized radiation field are rigorously established. By tracking the macroscopic one-particle density matrix $\kappa_T$ through a nonlinear resonance cascade, it is demonstrated that radiative relaxation irreversibly depletes all excited trap modes, even when the initial macroscopic state $\kappa_0$ is genuinely mixed. Here $\kappa_T$ is an average, with respect to a de Finetti measure $\mu_0$, over mean-field particle-field orbits, so that the mixedness of $\kappa_0$ reflects a statistical ensemble of orbits. Under the assumptions of a non-vanishing initial ground state component and strictly positive downward Fermi-Golden-Rule rates, strong trace-norm convergence to a pure condensate is proven, $$ \lim_{T\to\infty} \| \kappa_T-|\chi_0\rangle\langle\chi_0| \|_{\mathfrak{S}_1(\mathfrak{h})} = 0 \, . $$ Furthermore, the von Neumann entropy of the macroscopic one-particle density matrix is shown to vanish asymptotically, $$ \lim_{T\to\infty}S[\kappa_T]=0 \, , $$ without any claim of monotonicity in $T$. Thus, any initially mixed, positive-entropy state ($0<S[\kappa_0]<\infty$) is purified to the ground state $|\chi_0\rangle\langle\chi_0|$. For the proof, we derive the Hartree hierarchy of the coupled system of bosons and photons from the finite-$N$ BBGKY hierarchy of the microscopic quantum many-body system, establishing trace-norm convergence in the mean-field limit as $N\to\infty$. The limits are taken successively; first $N\to\infty$, then the weak-coupling limit, and finally $T\to\infty$. Although the global particle-field evolution remains unitary, the macroscopic one-particle state converges to a pure state as energy and correlations are continuously radiated into the dispersive field.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Chen, Ali Mezher

item.title: Haagerup-Izumi modular data from hyperbolic words: S-fold TQFTs, central charge, torsion and the Bethe vacua
item.description: arXiv:2610.18512v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The modular data of the doubles of the Haagerup--Izumi categories is a grafting of two finite metric groups (conjectured by Evans--Gannon, proved for untwisted categories by Gannon--Schopieray--Yadav). Gang and Kim found non-unitary modular data of this shape in the topological twist of rank-$0$ $S$-fold theories, from the Bethe vacua of an abelianised gauge theory. The aim is to understand rigorously the significance of the handle-gluing and fibering operators, and to construct the Bethe vacua. For every hyperbolic once-punctured-torus monodromy $\varphi$, a word in $L$ and $R$, the two groups are $A_\mp=\coker(\varphi\mp1)$, with the torsion linking forms of the mapping tori of $\varphi$ and $-\varphi$. Over all words of trace $m^2+2$ these forms reproduce the Evans--Gannon table of Q-systems, one printed entry being corrected, and the distinct modular data in the list of Gannon--Schopieray--Yadav. The Bethe data are given in closed form by the word: the level matrix, the positive vacuum, $c_{\eff}=\#L$, and the handle-gluing values $2^{\#L}\lambda^{\pm1}|A_-||A_+|$ at the identity classes, $\lambda$ the stretch factor. Each kernel vector of $\varphi\mp1$ modulo $|A_\mp|$ at which an explicit trigonometric formula does not vanish gives a solution of the Bethe equations in closed form. Under the half-index dictionary, with the unit in the class of $\sigma V^*$, $c\equiv\#L-6\#R\pmod{24}$.
item.dc:creator: David E Evans

item.title: Inverse eigenvalue problem for discrete three-diagonal Schroedinger operator and the continuum limit in Tikhonov regularization approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.18734v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the present article the self-contained derivation of main formulas of the inverse eigenvalue problem for the Sturm-Liouville operator is given on the base of its discrete approximation and the subsequent transition to the limit of the continuum coordinate. In doing so, we adhere to Tikhonov concept, where the discrete approximation is performed as a regularization of the ill-posed operator problem. While the continuum limit for the three-diagonal matrix Hamiltonian is impossible as such, following the Tikhonov procedure leads not to a limit for the potential matrix itself, but rather for a certain combination of the matrix elements, and this limit is precisely the desired potential in the continuum case.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir M. Chabanov

item.title: Finite temperature Fredholm determinants for dynamical correlation functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.18750v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of finite-temperature dynamical Fredholm determinants using effective form factors. The method expresses these asymptotics as a functional of an effective phase shift. We determine its two branches on either side of a quadratic stationary point and the transition profile joining them. The profile is expressed through parabolic-cylinder functions. Its connection to the high-temperature Gaussian $\beta$ ensemble fixes the finite normalization, in agreement with an independent Riemann--Hilbert analysis. We also show that the leading exponential asymptotics suffice to recover the Euler-scale prediction of generalized hydrodynamics for the dynamical structure factor of hard rods.
item.dc:creator: Oleksandr Gamayun

item.title: Computation of unknotting numbers: which knot breaks the Bernhard-Jablan Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2609.09861v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine $2,540$ unknotting numbers of prime knots with at most $13$ crossings, that are unknown in the KnotInfo snapshot of 9 September 2026. The lower-bound calculations use Heegaard Floer correction-term obstructions and Greene's spanning-tree model. We also give explicit crossing-change constructions for upper bounds. For $959$ alternating knots with range $[2,3]$, we verify that no crossing change in a minimal diagram gives a knot of unknotting number one. We determine the unknotting numbers of all four knots in Brittenham and Hermiller's construction and thereby identify 13n3370 as an explicit counterexample to the original Bernhard-Jablan conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Seong-Jin Lee

item.title: Spacetimes of maximal proper acceleration and muon mean lifetime
item.description: arXiv:2609.25903v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, it is shown that in spacetimes of maximal proper acceleration, there is a reduction of the mean lifetime of the muon. We consider several candidates for the maximal proper acceleration. For all of them, the induced corrections are small, but for the case when the maximal proper acceleration is identified with the Schwinger's acceleration, the effect is detectable in future muon collider facilities.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: International Journal of Geometric Methods in Modern Physics Vol. 24, No. 02, 2650124 (2027)
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Gallego Torrom\'e

item.title: Predictive Holonomy and Minimal Completion of Coarse Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.13951v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A coarse description of a dynamical system generally fails to evolve autonomously: evolving and coarse-graining in different orders gives different predictions, and the compressed propagator fails the semigroup law. We show that this path dependence is the observable boundary of missing state. For a finite continuous-time Markov chain with generator $L$, coarse channel $C$, and stochastic section $R$ satisfying $CR=I$, define $P=RC$, $Q=I-P$, and $K=CLR$. The exact coarse propagator $T_t=C\mathrm{e}^{tL}R$ obeys a Volterra equation with memory kernel $\mathcal{M}(t)=CLQ\,\mathrm{e}^{tQLQ}\,QLR$. Every memory jet $\mathcal{M}^{(k)}(0)$ is recursively recoverable from the short-time derivatives of $T_t$ alone. The rank of the block Hankel operator $\mathbb{H}_{\infty}=(\mathcal{M}^{(i+j)}(0))_{i,j\geq 0}$ is exactly the smallest number of auxiliary linear state variables required to turn the coarse dynamics into an exact autonomous, time-homogeneous system. A minimal completion is constructible by Ho--Kalman factorization and is unique up to similarity. If $d=\min\{k:\mathcal{M}^{(k)}(0)\neq 0\}$, then every smooth classical $f$-divergence generically scales as $t^{2d+4}$. Exact Markov examples realize exponents $4,6,8$ and closure ranks $1,2,3$. We also derive finite-sample singular-value certificates for hidden predictive coordinates, including a matrix-Bernstein bound with intrinsic-variance control. Finally, histories are identified when they induce the same future law under every admissible intervention, yielding the minimal counterfactual predictive state. The results turn coarse-graining into a constructive state-completion problem and separate ordinary linear realization from the harder requirement of a positive or Markov realization.
item.dc:creator: Maxim V. Churilov

item.title: SIREN: A nonlinear Rankine-source boundary element solver for the stationary motion of a marine vehicle in calm water
item.description: arXiv:2610.14027v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: SIREN (Ship Inviscid Resistance and Elevation eNgine) is a Rankine-source panel solver for the steady wave resistance of a ship, in the tradition of Dawson's method. The free-surface condition is linearised about a base flow, and the linearisation is iterated. In the present formulation the base flow is the solution of a Neumann problem on the actual boundary: sources on the entire hull, wet and dry, and on the free surface panels, with impermeability imposed on both, so that the free surface acts as a rigid lid at the position it currently occupies. This replaces the classical double-body flow, whose image about z=0 is meaningful only for a flat surface and a hull cut at z=0, and it removes the need for desingularised free-surface panels. In the non-linear iteration the free-surface panels are moved rigidly in the vertical to the relaxed wave elevation at their centroid, the hull panels are marked wet or dry against the moved surface, and the base flow is recomputed on the moved geometry; impermeability applies to the whole hull regardless of this marking, which is used only to select which panels enter the force integral, and under-relaxation is confined to the passes where the non-linear correction accumulates without being reset. The radiation condition is imposed by a one-row upstream shift of the collocation points, and the wave resistance is obtained by pressure integration and, independently, by transverse wave-cut analysis.
item.dc:creator: Daniele Peri

item.title: Equivariant Seiberg-Witten equations on Hermitian symmetric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.14045v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We formulate and solve a $G$-equivariant analogue of the Seiberg-Witten equations on any irreducible Hermitian symmetric space $G/K$. We use a canonical $K$-invariant form to define a twisted Hodge operator generalising self-duality to higher dimensions. The resulting equivariant Seiberg-Witten equations arise, for a compact $G/K$, as conditions for the absolute minima of an energy functional. Their linear part has a representation theoretic interpretation: the same Weyl group data control the highest-weight realisation of the positive Dirac kernel in the compact case and its discrete-series realisation on the non-compact dual. This space of harmonic spinors collapses almost entirely by the quadratic conditions of the monopole equation. In the compact case, the equivariant moduli set, when non-empty, is a single gauge class, identifying with the $G$-invariant part of Bradlow's trichotomy for vortices, while in the non-compact case, every irreducible solution sits outside the discrete series.
item.dc:creator: Rafailia-Persefoni Tsiavou

item.title: An Explicit Bound for the First Dirichlet Eigenvalue via Two Moments
item.description: arXiv:2610.14069v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $(M^n,g)$, $n\ge2$, be a compact connected Riemannian manifold with smooth nonempty boundary, $\operatorname{Ric}_M\ge(n-1)Kg$ for $K>0$, and nonnegative outward boundary mean curvature. We derive an explicit algebraic lower bound $B_\eta$ for the first Dirichlet eigenvalue from Kasue's mixed inradius model. With $R$ the inradius and $s=4KR^2/\pi^2$, the bound involves one square root and approximates the model eigenvalue with relative error $O_n(s^4)$ as $s\downarrow0$ for fixed $n$. The construction uses the first two moments of a positive representation of the averaged model potential and a sharp pointwise corrector estimate. For the chosen spectral transfer, the first two moments determine an optimal bound. We also show that the model eigenvalue is the geometric infimum at fixed $(n,K,R)$. For $0<s<1$, it is approached by smooth collapsing balls with sectional curvature at least $K$ and totally geodesic boundary. At the maximal inradius, the model value is attained by the round hemisphere. The bound strictly improves the variance refinement throughout $0<s\le1$. We also give a direct algebraic comparison with an optimized power-test benchmark.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Sch\"urmann

item.title: Prelocality No-Go Theorems and Exactly Solvable Relational History Hamiltonians
item.description: arXiv:2610.14081v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Exact permutation covariance does not itself supply a sparse metric geometry. For permutation-covariant, full-support $k$-body interaction orbits, the incident interaction norm scales as $\binom{N-1}{k-1}|J_N|\|h\|$; such orbits cannot have uniformly finite range in metrics of diverging diameter. A permutation-invariant Hamiltonian diagonal in the graph basis has ground-state multiplicity at least $N!/|\mathrm{Aut}(G)|$ whenever $G$ is a ground graph. We give a quantitative version for approximately symmetric energies, together with fixed-radius connectivity and unitary-isometry obstructions. The trace-distance asymmetry of an arbitrary state also bounds its probability of selecting one labeled graph. We then construct two exactly solvable finite relational history Hamiltonians. A cyclic clock with a reversible incidence update has a unique ground state; gauge reduction yields a cycle Laplacian with a rank-one pin and the exact gap $\Delta_{N,L}=E_* (1-\cos\theta_L)$, where $\tan(L\theta_L/2)=1/\sin\theta_L$ and $0<\theta_L<\pi/L$. In particular, $\Delta_{N,L}/E_*=\pi^2/(2L^2)-2\pi^2/L^3+O(L^{-4})$, independently of the number of vertices. In an alternative order-free architecture, one clock qubit per unordered pair gives commuting four-local terms, $2^N$ ground states and a size-independent gap $E_*(1-1/\sqrt2)$. A fixed-weight control penalty selects $\binom Nq$ ground states without reducing the gap. These exact finite results expose clock and locality resource tradeoffs; they do not establish an emergent geometric phase.
item.dc:creator: Maxim V. Churilov

item.title: Exact SU($N$) symmetry resolution of bosonic Hubbard models: general boson-fermion mappings and flat-band singlet-cluster states
item.description: arXiv:2610.14183v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show how to perform exact diagonalization of SU($N$)-symmetric Bose-Hubbard models separately in each irreducible representation of SU($N$), by exploiting the Howe duality between U($L$) and U($N$). Three structural consequences follow for any lattice and any Hamiltonian built from the U($L$) generators: (i) the spectrum in a given orbital sector is independent of $N$ and of the particle statistics, (ii) the canonical partition functions for bosons and fermions obey the exact identity $Z_{\mathrm{b}}(-N)=(-1)^{N_\mathrm{b}}Z_{\mathrm{f}}(N)$, (iii) with unfrustrated hopping the groundstate is always a color ferromagnet, so that the color-resolved method we introduce is useful to study excited sectors, frustrated lattices and finite temperatures. As applications, we first derive the finite-temperature phase diagram of attractive SU($N$) bosons on few-site rings at large $N$ for arbitrary filling. We then show the emergence of singlet-cluster states from frustrated hopping, the counterpart of fermionic ferromagnetism, with the example of the sawtooth and kagome lattice.
item.dc:creator: Lo\"ic Herviou

item.title: Example of exponential many collisions of identical hard disks in the plane
item.description: arXiv:2610.14282v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $ \operatorname{MaxCol}(n,d) $ denote the maximal number of nonsimultaneous elastic collisions among $n$ identical hard balls moving freely in $\mathbb{R}^d$. We give a planar construction with exponential lower bound with respect to $n$: $ \operatorname{MaxCol}(n,2)\geq 2^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}, \quad n\geq3 $.
item.dc:creator: Hongda Qiu

item.title: Haagerup conformal field theory at central charge eight
item.description: arXiv:2610.14441v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a chiral algebra $U$ of central charge eight inside the lattice vertex operator algebra $V_{E_6\oplus A_2}$. It is generated by two commuting affine $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ current algebras at levels $1$ and $39$, the stress tensor of the lattice theory, and a single weight-two field built from three lattice exponentials. We announce that $U$ is strongly rational and completely unitary, and that $Rep(U)$ is equivalent, as a unitary ribbon category, to the Drinfeld center $Z(\mathcal{H}_3)$ of the Haagerup fusion category $\mathcal{H}_3$. Its characters are the $\gamma=0$ Evans--Gannon vector. From $U$ we obtain a diagonal full CFT, and also a holomorphic $E_8$ extension on which $\mathcal{H}_3$ acts by topological defects.
item.dc:creator: Tzu-Chen Huang

item.title: Harmonic Reduction of Spin-Coupled Grover Walks on Hypercubes via Quantum Bernoulli Noises
item.description: arXiv:2610.14467v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider spin-coupled Grover walks on hypercubes within the framework of quantum Bernoulli noises (QBN). We identify parity-dependent harmonic subspaces generated by the central Hamming layers: in even dimension they give a fixed-point subspace, whereas in odd dimension the walk reduces on the harmonic subspace to an explicit eight-dimensional reduced dynamics. Using symmetric-group representation theory, we characterize the corresponding isotypic structure and determine the reduced spectrum. The harmonic reduction also yields explicit long-time probability behavior and shows that the resulting states may occupy an asymptotically vanishing fraction of the hypercube while still spanning its full Hamming diameter.
item.dc:creator: Ce Wang

item.title: Cetraro lectures on integrable systems and moduli spaces of curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.14608v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In these lecture notes we review some constructions and results on the relation between topology of the moduli space of stable curves and integrable systems of evolutionary PDEs.
item.dc:creator: Alexandr Buryak, Paolo Rossi

item.title: Classical Communication Helps Single-Shot Quantum Compression
item.description: arXiv:2610.14785v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Free classical communication can yield an unbounded single-shot saving in quantum compression, even though it leaves the asymptotic rate of an i.i.d. source unchanged. At every fixed error in $(0,1)$, we exhibit sources whose unassisted compression cost is arbitrarily large, yet a single qubit suffices with classical communication and no preshared entanglement. We establish this separation by determining the exact optimal source fidelity for compression through an $m$-dimensional noiseless quantum channel, with and without free classical communication, while preserving correlations with an inaccessible reference. Without classical assistance, the optimal fidelity is exactly the Ky Fan norm $\|\rho\|_{(m)}$, the sum of the $m$ largest eigenvalues of the source state. With classical assistance, we obtain an explicit spectral threshold formula and a protocol attaining it. Classical communication strictly improves fidelity whenever $m$ is smaller than the source rank. The corresponding compression costs are two smoothed versions of the log-rank entropy, also called max-entropy: trace-distance smoothing under local operations and quadratic smoothing under LOCC. For i.i.d. copies of a fixed source with positive entropy variance, however, the two costs have identical first-, second-, and third-order asymptotic terms. For nonlattice spectra, we determine the constant-order advantage: classical communication saves $\log_2(e)-1$ bits per block asymptotically, and the ratio of assisted to unassisted minimum communication dimensions converges to $2/e$.
item.dc:creator: Omri Farber, Gilad Gour

item.title: Global Well-Posedness and Uniform Long-Time Control for a Class of Periodic NLS-Dysthe Equations
item.description:
arXiv:2610.14786v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a class of periodic NLS-Dysthe (NLS-Dy) equations, also referred to as higher-order nonlinear Schr"odinger equations (HNLS), of the form $i\partial_t u+a\partial_x^2u+b|u|^2u+i\varepsilon(c\partial_x^3u+d|u|^2\partial_xu+eu^2\partial_x\overline{u})=0$ with $ x\in\mathbb T$, $a,b,c,d,e\in\mathbb R$, $abc
eq0$, and $\varepsilon>0$. For $0<\varepsilon\ll1$, equations of this type arise as higher-order modulation models for some nonlinear dispersive PDEs, including the Klein-Gordon equation and the Serre-Green-Naghdi equation modeling the evolution of nonlinear shallow water waves. We prove local well-posedness in $H^s(\mathbb T)$ for $s>3/2$ for arbitrary admissible coefficients, and establish an $H^1$ continuation criterion for $s\ge2$. In the parameter regime $e
eq0$, a lower-order conservation law provides uniform $H^1$ control and, together with the continuation criterion, yields global well-posedness for $s\ge2$. This result does not require the non-resonance condition appearing in Takaoka's periodic theory, while the condition $e
eq0$ naturally arises in the modulation setting considered here. Finally, motivated by the long-time regime relevant for modulation, we establish uniform long-time control without imposing a smallness assumption on the initial datum. Using the conservation laws of cubic NLS and their invariance under the commuting complex mKdV flow, we obtain uniform $H^s$ bounds on time intervals of order $\varepsilon^{-1}$ for integer $s\ge2$. For non-integer real $s\ge2$, the maximal $H^s$ solution exists on the same time scale, while uniform control is obtained at a lower regularity, with a loss of less than one derivative.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Belloni, Filippo Giuliani

item.title: On best approximation and estimates of Bohr--Favard type on the sphere for functions with bounded Laplacian
item.description: arXiv:2610.14811v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the best constants in estimates of the $L^\infty$ norm of functions on the sphere with bounded Laplacian whose first spherical harmonic components vanish. In every dimension $d\geq2$, these constants are expressed through weighted $L^1$ extremal polynomials. On $S^2$ the constant is an explicit positive series, and the best coefficient of $n^{-2}$ is $7\zeta(3)/4$. On $S^3$ the best coefficient of $n^{-2}$ is a positive integral involving the H\"ormander--Bernhardsson extremal function. In higher dimensions the rescaled extremal polynomials converge to weighted entire extremals, which give asymptotic formulas for the Bohr constants on $S^4$ and $S^6$. The most unexpected and, in our view, interesting observation is that, for every fixed $n\geq2$ on $S^2$ and $S^3$, the constants in best approximation estimates are \emph{strictly smaller} than the corresponding Bohr--Favard constants.
item.dc:creator: Alexey Solyanik

item.title: Lifts of symmetries to minimal nondegenerate extensions are unique up to fermion attachment
item.description: arXiv:2610.14847v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Gauging fermion parity in a $(2+1)$-dimensional fermionic topological order requires lifting its symmetries to the resulting bosonic theory. We give a direct tensor-categorical proof that, for a slightly degenerate braided fusion category $\mathcal{C}$ and a fixed minimal nondegenerate extension ${\cal E}$, the restriction homomorphism $r\colon\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{LR}}(\mathcal{E})\to \operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{LR}}(\mathcal{C})$ on classes of complex-linear locality-respecting (LR) braided autoequivalences is surjective with central kernel $\mathbb{Z}/2$, generated by fermion attachment. Thus each symmetry class has exactly two LR lift classes, related by attaching the fermion to every vortex. We apply graded Morita theory to reduce the kernel to two module types on the vortex sector, corresponding to tensoring with the vacuum or the fermion. We then prove relative rigidity to show that each type determines a unique LR class, which are distinguished by fermionic self-braiding even when their actions on simple-object labels coincide. We prove surjectivity by extending graph algebras in $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{rev}}\boxtimes\mathcal{C}$ to Lagrangian algebras in $\mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{rev}}\boxtimes\mathcal{E}$. Our results require neither unitarity nor a ribbon structure. We illustrate the lifting ambiguity in the Laughlin state, the $SO(3)_3$ theory and the Ising topological order.
item.dc:creator: Ran Luo, Jiahua Tian

item.title: Overlap distributions under the Gibbs measure of a Haar model of $\log|\zeta|$ on and near the critical line
item.description: arXiv:2610.14901v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the Gibbs measure of $H(h) = \Re\sum_{p^{j} \leq X}U_{p}^{j}/(j p^{j(\sigma + i h)})$, a random field modeling large values of the log-modulus of the Riemann zeta function on and near the critical line, where the $U_{p}$ are independent and uniformly distributed on the complex unit circle. Writing $t = \log \log T$, the cutoff $X$ and real part $\sigma$ may vary with $T$ subject to $T^{1/t^{\Phi}} \leq X \leq T^{1/t^{\phi}}$ and $0 \leq \sigma - 1/2 \leq C_{\sigma}t^{\Phi}/\log T$, for fixed $\Phi \geq \phi > 1/2$ and $C_{\sigma} > 0$. On $I_{\theta} = [ - (\log T)^{\theta},(\log T)^{\theta}]$, define the Gibbs measure $G_{\beta,\sigma,T}^{\mathrm{H}}(\mathrm{d}h) := e^{\beta H(h)}\mathrm{d}h/\int_{I_{\theta}}e^{\beta H(h')}\mathrm{d}h'$. For every fixed $\theta > - 1$ and inverse temperature $\beta > 0$, the limiting joint distributions of correlations (overlaps) among points sampled from this measure are determined after averaging over the Haar phases. At and below $\beta_{c}(\theta) = 2\sqrt{1 + (\theta \vee 0)}$, the limiting two-overlap distribution is concentrated at $q_{0} = |\theta \wedge 0|$. Above this threshold, it assigns masses $\beta_{c}(\theta)/\beta$ and $1 - \beta_{c}(\theta)/\beta$ to $q_{0}$ and $1$, respectively, and the limiting joint overlap distribution is described by a Poisson-Dirichlet process of parameter $\beta_{c}(\theta)/\beta$. Approximate Ghirlanda-Guerra identities are shown to hold uniformly for bounded deterministic functions of the sampled positions. This paper is the first in a series devoted to extending these results to $\log|\zeta|$ near the critical line.
item.dc:creator: Fr\'ed\'eric Ouimet

item.title: DisCo Algebra: Why Disintegration and Combination Are Not Inverses
item.description: arXiv:2610.15006v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present DisCo algebra---a compositional framework for joint probability built from a symmetric cooperad (disintegration) and a symmetric operad (combination) on the bare family $\mathcal{P}_n=\mathrm{Prob}([0,1]^n)$. No probability integral transform, no external summary functions, no enrichment of objects with conditional kernels. The disintegration side uses block-wise joint CDFs as intrinsic, measure-determined 1D summaries, yielding a lossy compression. The combination side reads the same summaries and reconstructs via regular conditional measures, yielding a lossless embedding. We prove that combination followed by disintegration is the identity on admissible inputs, but disintegration followed by combination is not---the information loss is exactly the conditional KL divergence between the true conditional distribution and the conditionally independent product. This asymmetry reveals a hard limit on how much cross-block dependence can be captured by scalar block summaries.
item.dc:creator: Xuexing Lu

item.title: Plane wave representation for wave scattering on a sphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.15121v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Motivated by three-dimensional wave diffraction by conical shapes, we consider the two-dimensional problem of wave scattering on the real sphere $\mathcal{S}^2$ resulting from a point-source incidence on a scatterer $\mathbb{S}$. Using the recently introduced notion of plane waves on $\mathcal{S}^2$ as well as recent results on the Laplace--Beltrami Green's function $G$ on $\mathcal{S}^2$, we derive three plane-wave representations for the scattered field $u$. We then explain how $u$ can be analytically continued to the complexified sphere $\mathcal{S}^2_{\mathbb{c}}$. This allows us to formulate a complexified version of Green's third identity, and to provide a characterisation of complex sources. All our results are then used to draw strong analogies between planar and spherical scattering problems, notably through the introduction of directivities.
item.dc:creator: Valentin D. Kunz, Andrey V. Shanin, Raphael C. Assier

item.title: The R\'enyi area law conjecture is false below $\alpha=1$ in high dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.15199v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Area laws express the expectation that entanglement in gapped quantum ground states scales with a boundary rather than a volume. In one dimension this holds for every R\'enyi entropy, and the R\'enyi area-law conjecture asserts the same in higher dimensions for each fixed $0<\alpha<1$. Here we disprove this conjecture in every spatial dimension two and higher. We construct finite-range Hamiltonians with fixed local dimension, bounded interaction strength, unique ground states and a uniform spectral gap, whose ground states exhibit volume-law R\'enyi entanglement while obeying a von Neumann area law and remaining connected to product states through uniformly gapped local paths. The mechanism is error-space complexity: locally identifiable components of arbitrarily small weight can encode states with high entanglement complexity. We also establish the worst-case rank-error trade-off for approximate ground-state projectors, a key tool in one-dimensional area-law proofs. At fixed gap, the optimal Schmidt rank at projection error $\epsilon$ across a planar cut of cross-section $A$ scales as $\exp[\tilde{\Theta}((A\log\epsilon^{-1})^{2/3})]$ when $\log\epsilon^{-1}\gtrsim A$. Thus $\alpha=1$ is the sharp threshold for a universal R\'enyi area law within this adiabatically connected class.
item.dc:creator: Tomotaka Kuwahara

item.title: Type $B$- and $C$- trigonometric weight functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.15344v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce and study trigonometric weight functions of type $B$ and type $C$ arising from integrable lattice models. These functions give $q$-deformations of the factorial $K$-theoretic Schur $P$- and $Q$-functions of Ikeda and Naruse, with the $P$-functions specialized to the type $B$ case. We realize them as specializations of partition functions of a six-vertex model with triangular boundary conditions and derive their algebraic properties using the Yang-Baxter equation and properties of the $R$- and $K$-matrices. We introduce normalized weight functions and establish diagonal evaluation formulas, divisibility properties, and bounds on Newton polytopes analogous to those in type $A$, together with recursive relations and stability. We further derive branching formulas relating these functions to type $A$ weight functions, and prove equal-cardinality orthogonality and all-cardinality biorthogonality relations.
item.dc:creator: Kohei Motegi

item.title: Numerical Modeling of a Metallic Alloy Droplet Impact, Solidification, and Macrosegregation
item.description: arXiv:2610.15381v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For the first time, we study the effects of mass transfer on alloy droplet impact, solidification, and solute non-homogeneity or MacroSegregation (MS). For this purpose, a multi-physics model, including fully-coupled hydrodynamics of multiphase flow, wetting, conjugate heat transfer, phase change, and mass transfer, is established and validated carefully across several benchmarks. In addition, a concentration-flux-correction algorithm is proposed to conserve the solute mass within the droplet at the numerical discretization level. The validated model is subsequently used to explore the impact and solidification of an alloy droplet. The results show that accounting for mass transfer and solute transport improves the prediction of the dynamics of a solidifying splat, in a consistent manner with experimental observations, while this effect has been neglected in all previous studies. The analysis demonstrates that this improvement results from the flow sensitivity to the mushy region thickness, which is regulated by local solute concentration through the solidus and liquidus temperatures. Furthermore, analyses of the MS map identify several critical segregation regions most susceptible to defect initiation, such as cracking, including a long negatively segregated vein within the lamella, formed by the severe advective flow through the mush in the middle stages of the impact, a positively segregated region near the rim of the splat, appearing as a result of hook formation, and a major positively segregated zone at the top of the rim, which develops following the accumulation of the solute-rich melt sustained by washout from the lamella.
item.dc:creator: Ehsan Amani, Ali Moinirad

item.title: Spectral geometry of saturated Fell bundles
item.description: arXiv:2610.15395v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal B=(B_g)_{g\in G}$ be a saturated Fell bundle over a countable discrete group, equipped with a spectral triple. We give explicit sufficient conditions for lifting this triple to the reduced cross-sectional C\Star-algebra $C_r^*(\mathcal B)$. Using finite projective realizations of the homogeneous Morita equivalence $B_e$-bimodules, we transport the base Dirac operator to the individual fibres and assemble the resulting operators into a fibrewise Dirac operator. We introduce a spectral-regularity condition ensuring bounded commutators and give a sufficient criterion in terms of uniform derivative bounds on smooth factor-system data. Combining the fibrewise operator with a length operator associated with a proper translation-bounded matrix-valued length function yields the lifted spectral triple. When $B_e$ is separable, the lifted triple, with a suitable grading, represents the Kasparov product of the vertical class with the class of the unit-fibre triple. We also establish a summability criterion and sufficient conditions for stability under central cocycle twisting. A range of examples illustrates the scope of the construction, including twisted crossed products, free compact Abelian actions, and Fell bundles with nonfree homogeneous fibres.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Wagner

item.title: New topological phase transitions in $\kappa$-deformed $\phi^4$ lattice models
item.description: arXiv:2610.15644v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper explores topological phase transitions in the momentum space of the $\kappa$-deformed $\phi^4$ lattice model within the mean-field approximation. We show that the double-well structure of the momentum space gives rise to degenerate momentum states at high energies and that this change is marked by a phase transition. We investigate this transition using both numerical and analytical methods, with the analytical approach based primarily on singularity theory. Our numerical analysis shows that the energy at which the topological phase transition occurs is related to the noncommutative parameter by the simple power law $E \sim 1/\alpha^{4}$. By mapping the constant-energy-level surface to the $A_{3}$ singularity, we obtain the same result analytically. We also present results unique to noncommutative systems, showing that the fraction of particles in degenerate momentum states has a nonzero commutative limit. As a nonperturbative effect, this result provides a testable prediction for the existence of noncommutative spacetime.
item.dc:creator: Adith A, A. Bhagwat

item.title: Non-Stationary Quantum Systems Associated with Stationary Scattering in One Dimension
item.description: arXiv:2610.15655v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stationary scattering admits a dynamical formulation in which the scattering data are extracted from the evolution operator for an effective non-stationary and non-unitary quantum system. This provides a mathematical method of solving scattering problems. We consider the possibility of realizing such a quantum system and relating the scattering information to outcomes of quantum measurements performed on it. To this end, we examine stationary scattering problems in one dimension where the scattering data consist of reflection and transmission amplitudes and the corresponding effective quantum system is a non-unitary two-level system. The states of this system identify points in a Bloch sphere $S^2$ and their evolution yields trajectories in $S^2$. Quantum measurements turn out to be capable of providing information about the reflection amplitudes. We identify configurations displaying reflectionlessness with situations where one or both of the poles of $S^2$ undergo cyclic evolutions. Spectral singularities and coherent perfect absorption correspond to dynamical spin flips which map one of the poles of $S^2$ to the other.
item.dc:creator: Ali Mostafazadeh, Alireza Shariati Joni

item.title: An optimization problem for $\delta'$ leaky stars
item.description: arXiv:2610.15771v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider singular Schr\"odinger operators with an attractive $\delta'$ interaction of strength $\beta$ supported by a star graph and prove that the ground-state eigenvalue is uniquely maximized by stars of the maximum symmetry. Two different proofs are presented, one for an even number of edges using a comparison to the $\delta$ interaction star, the other general based on Birman-Schwinger technique.
item.dc:creator: Pavel Exner

item.title: Planar intrusions from a narrow, jet-like source in a linearly stratified ambient
item.description: arXiv:2610.16011v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present two and three dimensional direct numerical simulations of planar intrusions injected from a continuously supplied, narrow source into a linearly stratified ambient at the level of neutral buoyancy. The evolution passes through three phases. A laminar leading vortex dipole first advances at constant speed with a varicose wave train behind it; the trailing jet then undergoes a sinuous instability whose initial growth rate and wavelength agree with inviscid unstratified planar-jet theory evaluated on the local jet; the flow finally relaxes into a buoyancy-controlled wedge whose area grows linearly in time. Three-dimensional simulations show that the transition remains organized by the planar instability, while three-dimensionality reshapes the near-source region into a slowly evolving, actively mixing zone that entrains an additional twenty to one hundred percent of the source flux depending on source width. Rescaled with this measured effective flux, the downstream intrusion collapses reasonably well onto the similarity solution for a wide-source intrusion.
item.dc:creator: Hai Duc Vu, Murray Rudman, Anja Slim

item.title: Finiteness of planar central configurations of five bodies for all positive masses: On Smale's sixth problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.16107v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that for every choice of five positive masses the planar five-body problem has only finitely many central configurations up to rotation, translation and scaling. This answers Smale's sixth problem for five bodies. Albouy and Kaloshin proved the statement for all masses outside a closed algebraic subset of codimension two of the mass space. We keep their classification of singular sequences and replace the construction of the exceptional set by a direct exclusion: we use finite boundary charts for seven of the eight diagrams that can carry an unbounded four-product, and an exhaustive order census for Diagram 5. We derive the necessary mass conditions where needed and show that no germ with an unbounded four-product lies on a curve of normalized central configurations through a positive configuration. Five diagrams are excluded for all complex germs, two on curves through real configurations, and one on curves through positive configurations. Parts of the argument are computer-assisted: exact algebra, interval arithmetic and exact linear programming.
item.dc:creator: Zhe Chen, Zhicheng Tong

item.title: Probe Signatures of Quantum Chaos with Quantum Sensing
item.description: arXiv:2610.16181v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The spectral form factor (SFF), which is the Fourier transform of the two-point spectral correlation, is a fundamental diagnostics of quantum chaos. Nevertheless, its experimental detection in quantum many-body systems was less unexplored until recently. Here, we establish a relationship between the SFF with the quantum Fisher information (QFI) by means of quantum sensing protocols. Furthermore, when the eigenvalues and eigenstates of the disordered Hamiltonian are statistically independent, we prove that QFI is typical both in short and long timescales while numerics suggest that it is also typical at intermediate timescales, which ensures self-averaging of QFI. The self-averaging property renders the experimental measurement of QFI with our protocol less noisy in contrast with the direct measurement of SFF which is known to be non-self-averaging. Our results reveal an intriguing connection between quantum noise and the signatures of quantum chaos.
item.dc:creator: Isa\'ias Vallejo-Fabila, Jing Yang

item.title: A first order nonabelian antisymmetric tensor model with hidden higher symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2610.16250v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a nonabelian complex self-dual antisymmetric tensor model, with gauged internal symmetry, comprising a complex multiplet of massless self-dual antisymmetric tensor fields and its conjugate (interacting with massless Yang-Mills gauge fields). We build the model at the classical level, via a first order formulation, assigning local fields to a component expansion over the Dirac algebra and a basis of internal matrices, with Lorentz and gauge invariance ensured by tracing, and applying an appropriate bilinear form. The full expansion requires auxiliary place-holder fields, which are not potentials, but become curvatures (field strengths) after elimination via their algebraic equations of motion. The component expansion over the Dirac algebra is closed under multiplication by additional internal matrices, which are not gauge group generators, but mix internal components, and link auxiliary curvatures with potentials. The model is shown to be invariant under such transformations, and thus possesses a type of hidden internal symmetry. We analyze the specific case of gauge group $SU(2)\! \times \! U(1)$, and as higher symmetry candidates, we consider both the Lie group $SU(3)$ and the Lie superalgebra $SU(2/1)$ (with the additional matrices acting via Lie brackets, or graded Lie brackets, respectively).
item.dc:creator: Peter D. Jarvis, Jean Thierry-Mieg

item.title: Classical and Quantum Information Measures Characterizing Convertibility: An Axiomatic Approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.16267v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this PhD thesis, we take an axiomatic approach to studying multivariate divergences, which are measures of the information content of a tuple of classical or quantum states. These divergences are studied in the context of large-sample and catalytic convertibility of tuples of states. This type of convertibility is characterized by the ordering of an axiomatically defined family of divergences. In this thesis, we identify this family of divergences explicitly for two scenarios, one classical and one quantum. In the classical setting, we show that the relevant divergences are certain generalizations of the bivariate R\'enyi divergences. Unlike previous studies, we do not require the distributions to have the same support, yielding interesting new divergences. In the quantum setting, we consider pairs of classical-quantum states with pure component states, and find that majorization is characterized by all $\alpha$-$z$ relative entropies for $\alpha<1$. This demonstrates the first operational interpretation of these relative entropies.
item.dc:creator: Frits Verhagen

item.title: Regular-Zero Drinfeld-Sokolov Charges in Doubled Four-Dimensional Chern-Simons Theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.16271v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study classical local conserved charges obtained after finite-defect reduction of doubled four-dimensional Chern--Simons theory. At a finite simple zero, the inhomogeneous derivative term in the affine gauge transformation induced by the twist function vanishes, so the residue evaluations of the two Gaudin currents transform by the ordinary adjoint action. For each simple ideal, we use the Evans-compatible invariant tensors of the principal Drinfeld--Sokolov hierarchy as external algebraic input, construct local circle integrals, and treat the same-zero, distinct-zero, and mixed sectors separately, proving pairwise Poisson commutativity. Under the explicit assumptions of Stedman's simple-pole/simple-zero boundary Hamiltonian, the periodic trivial-monodromy sector, and boundary weights independent of phase-space variables, the reduced Hamiltonian decomposes term by term into finite-pole, infinity, finite-zero, and residual first-class-constraint contributions, which yields conservation of the constructed charges. We distinguish the finite-defect reduced space, the extended space carrying the residual constraint, and the physical quotient. The result is a conditional existence statement for a classical local Abelian Poisson subalgebra; we make no claim of functional independence, maximality, or Liouville completeness. Extensions to higher-order zeros and nontrivial monodromy sectors are outside the scope of this work.
item.dc:creator: Wentao Zeng, Yifan He, Xian Wu

item.title: Finite-time quantum equilibration from local correlations
item.description: arXiv:2610.16351v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An isolated quantum system evolves reversibly, yet a small subsystem can lose nearly all information about its initial state. Conserved quantities may retain some of this information, depending on how strongly they overlap with local observables. Here we consider a subsystem in an arbitrary initial state coupled to a maximally mixed bath. We show that the worst-input mean-square equilibration error, maximised over window origins, is bounded from above and below by the mean square of a complete local autocorrelation, with the stationary part subtracted. A correlation record over a finite interval therefore controls the equilibration error in every interval of the same length. The result allows arbitrary degeneracies of energies and gaps. We apply it to two static Hamiltonian families. For fixed spin subsystems in the one-particle sector of a bounded-range periodic clock, fixed-accuracy thermalisation is guaranteed on windows that grow only slightly faster than linearly with system size, despite exponentially small positive energies. A random commuting model with logarithmic interaction range retains an extensive set of conserved observables. Its expected mean-square error is bounded by a finite-size term and an inverse-time term. The inverse-time dependence is unavoidable because of the initial transient. These examples show how local relaxation can coexist with exact conservation laws and a finely spaced spectrum.
item.dc:creator: Piotr \'Cwikli\'nski

item.title: Quantum integrals II: Dominated and almost uniform convergence
item.description: arXiv:2610.16499v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: One main aim of our paper is to formulate noncommutative versions of the Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem in the setting of quantum integration theory on von Neumann algebras. Our starting point is a reformulation of classical dominated convergence in terms of weak* convergence. Using our recent sequential-continuity theorem, we obtain dominated convergence formulations for sequentially normal states and, under domination by a fixed bounded integrable majorant, for sequentially normal weights. Integrable, possibly unbounded, majorants are treated first in the tracial setting, then for arbitrary von Neumann algebras using Haagerup's L1 space, and finally using normal semifinite weights and their GNS representations. For any faithful normal semifinite weight $\phi$, weak* convergence of norm-bounded sequences is characterized by `integrating against' bounded positive integrable majorants. We also study noncommutative almost uniform and local almost uniform convergence. In particular, for norm-bounded sequences, local $\phi$-bilaterally almost uniform convergence implies weak* convergence and L1 convergence to 0 of $h^{1/2}(x_n-x)h^{1/2}$ for every positive Haagerup L1 density h, without assuming sigma-finiteness. We also prove a dominated convergence theorem in the predual: fixed positive order domination and Petz's almost uniform convergence imply convergence in the predual norm. We establish implications and equivalences among these convergence notions, connecting dominated convergence with tracial and nontracial integration.
item.dc:creator: David P. Blecher

item.title: Long-time asymptotics for the focusing coupled Kundu-Eckhaus equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.16564v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The focusing coupled Kundu-Eckhaus (CKE) equation extends the coupled nonlinear Schr\"odinger (CNLS) equation by adding quintic and derivative nonlinearities. We study the Cauchy problem for the focusing CKE equation with Schwartz initial data under the assumption of no discrete spectrum and no spectral singularities on the real axis. Based on the gauge equivalence between the focusing CKE and CNLS equations, we analyze the associated $3\times3$ matrix Riemann-Hilbert problem by the Deift-Zhou nonlinear steepest descent method. By establishing joint error estimates for the CNLS solution and the gauge phase, we obtain a uniform long-time asymptotic formula for the dispersive radiation of the CKE equation with an $O(t^{-1}\log t)$ remainder in bounded velocity cones.
item.dc:creator: Tianwei Qiu, Zhen Wang

item.title: The periodic Airy line ensembles
item.description: arXiv:2610.16611v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper we construct a one-parameter family of periodic Airy line ensembles $\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{per},R}$ for $R>0$ as weak scaling limits of Borodin's periodic Schur processes. We establish several properties of $\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{per},R}$, including a determinantal point process structure with an explicit correlation kernel. We also show that, after a parabolic shift and normalization, $\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{per},R}$ satisfies, on its domain $[-R/2,R/2]$, the same Brownian Gibbs property enjoyed by the usual Airy line ensemble. A main technical contribution of the paper is a general tightness criterion for determinantal line ensembles, which extends the argument used by Johansson in [Comm. Math. Phys. 242 (2003), 277-329] to prove a functional limit theorem for the discrete polynuclear growth model.
item.dc:creator: Evgeni Dimitrov, Samir Sarieddine, Zongrui Yang, Zhengye Zhou

item.title: Closed-form construction of exceptional points in a two-parametric PT-symmetric large-matrix model
item.description: arXiv:2610.16613v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stable bound states living on a discrete one-dimensional N-point lattice are assumed generated by a certain two-parametric PT symmetric potential $V=V(A,B)$.
