At any $N$, the coordinates $A=A^{(EP)}$ and $B=B^{(EP)}$ of the Kato's exceptional point (marking the phase-transition instant of the loss of stability) are defined, exactly, via roots of a certain elementary quartic polynomial.
item.dc:creator: Miloslav Znojil

item.title: Analytic Liouville Integrable Geodesic Flow Has Zero Entropy
item.description: arXiv:2610.16640v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper studies the topological entropy of real-analytic Liouville integrable Hamiltonian systems. We prove that the Hamiltonian flow on a compact connected regular energy hypersurface has zero topological entropy whenever a complete family of commuting real-analytic first integrals is generically independent in a connected neighborhood of that hypersurface. The proof uses finite normal expansions along minimal analytic carriers and an ergodic version of Ziglin's leading-term argument to obtain independent invariant normal polynomials, whose Poisson geometry makes all tangent Lyapunov exponents of the carriers vanish. In particular, we prove that a real-analytic Liouville integrable geodesic flow on a closed real-analytic Riemannian manifold has zero topological entropy, giving a positive answer to the conjecture proposed by Paternain in 1992.
item.dc:creator: Fei Liu, Xiaokai Liu, Xiang Zhang

item.title: Analytic Brill wave initial data with trapped surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.16773v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Since Brill's work of 1959, the conformal factor of finite-amplitude Brill waves, the axisymmetric and time-symmetric vacuum initial data on $\mathbb{R}^3$ that describe pure gravitational radiation, has been obtained only numerically, up to the most recent studies. Here an explicit one-parameter family of such data is constructed: the first explicit real-analytic, non-trivial, asymptotically flat vacuum initial data with trivial topology and a single end. The free metric function is a closed-form combination of elementary functions and a dilogarithm. The data have the toroidal conformal symmetry of Beig and Husa, and a change of variable of Natanzon type reduces every mode equation to the Gauss hypergeometric equation, so that the conformal factor is a series with explicit Gamma-function coefficients. The quantities that have so far required numerical work are thereby obtained exactly. A ground-state identity gives a sharp existence criterion: complete, asymptotically flat data exist precisely for $k<k_c=0.8048016772\ldots$, and the explicit series is identified with the unique variational solution. The ADM mass is an absolutely convergent digamma series, with $m/a=\pi k^2/10+O(k^3)$ for small amplitudes and an explicit residue at its critical divergence. Sufficiently strong waves contain trapped surfaces: it is proved that for $k$ close to $k_c$ the rescaled conformal factor converges to an explicit function and explicit tori and spheres become outer trapped, so that the data contain an apparent horizon. A numerical search, restricted to equatorially symmetric star-shaped surfaces, finds marginally trapped (minimal) spheres, which appear in a fold near $k=0.7670$. No thin-torus or weak-field approximation is used.
item.dc:creator: Piotr Koc

item.title: Small perturbations of the $2d$ classical Heisenberg model
item.description: arXiv:2610.16824v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Polyakov predicted in 1975 ([Pol75) that the spin $O(3)$-model (or classical Heisenberg model) should have exponential decay of correlations at all positive temperatures on $\mathbb{Z}^2$. Our main result is as follows: if we replace the Euclidean scalar product \begin{align*} \langle \sigma_i , \sigma_j\rangle = \sigma_i^x \sigma_j^x + \sigma_i^y \sigma_j^y + \sigma_i^z \sigma_j^z \end{align*} by the $\lambda$-modified scalar product \begin{align*} \langle \sigma_i , \sigma_j\rangle_\lambda := \sigma_i^x \sigma_j^x + \sigma_i^y \sigma_j^y + \lambda \sigma_i^z \sigma_j^z \end{align*} we show that for all $\lambda\in(-1,1)$, the $\mathbb{S}^2$ valued spin system with Gibbs measure $\exp(\beta \sum_{i\sim j} \langle \sigma_i,\sigma_j\rangle_\lambda)$ has power-law decay of correlations if $\beta$ is chosen large enough. This is the first evidence that arbitrary small smooth modifications of the classical Heisenberg model produce a BKT phase in $2d$. It was proved in the 1970s and 80s that there exist arbitrary small smooth modifications of the classical Heisenberg model which produce instead an Ising phase. In these work, they considered the regime $\lambda>1$ while in this paper, we consider the regime $\lambda<1$ which cannot be analyzed via reflection positivity and chessboard estimate. The two main ingredients used in our proof are the stability of the BKT phase under percolation type disorder ([DG25]) and weak regularity type properties of the groundstates or $\mathbb{S}^2$-valued harmonic maps associated to our $\lambda$-energy functional. This analytic step is interesting on its own. Finally, the exponential and power-law decay regime should be separated by a curve $\lambda \mapsto \beta_c(\lambda)$. We prove a rigorous lower bound in the case of the $\lambda$-anisotropic hemisphere model $\mathbb{S}^2_+$ which matches with RG flow predictions.
item.dc:creator: Christophe Garban, Nathan de Montgolfier

item.title: Regularity theory for lattice based harmonic maps and low temperature Gibbs measures of the spin-$O(N)$ model
item.description: arXiv:2610.16833v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The purpose of this note is twofold. First, we revisit the classical regularity theory of harmonic maps in the setting of maps defined on a lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ instead of $\mathbb{R}^d$ or some other manifold. The target space of our harmonic maps will be spheres $\mathbb{S}^{N-1}, N\geq 2$. A harmonic map $\sigma : \mathbb{Z}^d \to \mathbb{S}^{N-1}$ is a map which in any finite subgraph $\Lambda$ minimizes the internal Dirichlet energy $\frac 1 2 \sum_{i \sim j \in \Lambda} \|\sigma_i -\sigma_j\|^2$ given the boundary condition $\sigma_{|\partial \Lambda}$. One key difference between our setting and the continuum is that our main H\"older regularity statement in a large domain $\Lambda\subset \mathbb{Z}^{d=2}$ does not require any regularity assumption on the map $\sigma$ restricted to the boundary of the domain. For example, when $d=2$ and $N=3$, the H\"older regularity induced in the bulk of the domain holds uniformly in all boundary configurations $\sigma \in (\mathbb{S}^{2})^{\partial \Lambda}$ (this is in contrast with the continuum which requires extensions in suitable Sobolev spaces). The fact we obtain results uniformly in the boundary conditions allows us to extend our results for positive temperatures. Namely, as $T \searrow 0$, we obtain a local regularity theory for all infinite volume Spin $O(N)$ Gibbs measures, at least when $d=2$ and $N\geq 3$. We also discuss implications of our analysis in dimensions $d\geq 3$.
item.dc:creator: Christophe Garban, Nathan de Montgolfier

item.title: Iterated Graph Systems (III): Alexander-Orbach conjecture on hierarchical lattices
item.description: arXiv:2610.16875v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Can the Alexander-Orbach conjecture hold on hierarchical lattices? We construct Gromov-Hausdorff-Prokhorov scaling limits of critical percolation clusters on hierarchical lattices in the chemical metric and determine the typical spectral dimensions of the associated diffusions. These dimensions are dense in $(1,2)$; however, outside a narrow region in dimension space, we prove that the Alexander-Orbach conjecture fails on every hierarchical lattice under consideration.
item.dc:creator: Ziyu Neroli

item.title: Semiclassical Moser--Trudinger type inequalities for orthonormal families in $\mathbb{R}^2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.16922v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For $H^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$-orthonormal families $\{u_n\}_{n=1}^N$ with one-body density $\rho=\sum_{n=1}^N |u_n|^2$, we prove the whole-space endpoint Moser--Trudinger inequality $$ \int_{\mathbb{R}^2}\frac{e^{4\pi\rho(x)}-1-4\pi\rho(x)}{\rho(x)}\,dx \le C\left(N-1+\int_{\mathbb{R}^2}\rho(x)\,dx\right), $$ where the integrand on the left-hand side is defined to be zero on $\{x: \rho(x)=0\}$. We develop a heat-semigroup refinement of Rumin's density method to treat both the endpoint coefficient $4\pi$ and the whole-space setting. Our inequality is sharp in two respects: the optimality of the coefficient $4\pi$ and the linear growth in the rank $N$. Moreover, through a semiclassical analysis of the density generated by normalized Dirichlet eigenfunctions, we establish the collective asymptotic behaviors of the quantities appearing in the inequality in various regimes. These semiclassical behaviors show that the rank-dependent term $N-1$ on the right-hand side is indispensable.
item.dc:creator: Phuoc-Tai Nguyen, Tuan-Dat Tran

item.title: Asymptotic analysis of the confluent Dotsenko-Fateev system
item.description: arXiv:2610.16970v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Dotsenko-Fateev equation is a third-order linear ordinary differential equation studied in two-dimensional conformal field theory. We study the confluent Dotsenko-Fateev system, a rank-three system of linear ordinary differential equations obtained by confluence from a first-order system equivalent to the Dotsenko-Fateev equation. It has an irregular singular point at infinity, and its solutions admit double integral representations of confluent Selberg type. Using these representations, we construct sectorial fundamental solution matrices around infinity, establish their asymptotic expansions, and determine the associated Stokes matrices explicitly. We further study three aspects of the confluent Dotsenko-Fateev system: its equivalence to the degree-two polynomial reduction of the Schr\"{o}dinger equation for the quantum Painlev\'{e} equation of type V, its realization as a restriction of a confluent version of the linear Pfaffian system associated with Appell's hypergeometric function $F_4$, and its reduction to the trivial rank-one equation via integral transforms and a quadratic change of the independent variable.
item.dc:creator: Shunya Adachi

item.title: Half-space polynuclear growth: a multipoint Fredholm--Pfaffian formula
item.description: arXiv:2610.16989v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We derive a Fredholm-Pfaffian formula for the one-time multi-point transition probabilities of half-space polynuclear growth with any nonnegative boundary nucleation rate and general deterministic upper semi-continuous initial profiles. We prove the formula by showing that it satisfies an integral Kolmogorov equation with a unique bounded solution. We also discuss the formal 1:2:3 scaling limit of the kernel and its relation to the half-space KPZ fixed point.
item.dc:creator: Kailun Chen, Xincheng Zhang

item.title: Entanglement Sudden Death in Gapped Ground States
item.description: arXiv:2610.17038v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spatial sudden death of entanglement refers to the disappearance of quantum correlations between subsystems after a certain distance called the entanglement length. Specifically, given a density matrix $\rho_{ABC}$ on a tripartite system $ABC$ with $B$ spatially separating $A$ and $C$, the entanglement length is the distance $\ell(A,C)$ after which the reduced density matrix $\rho_{AC}$, given by tracing out the $B$ subsystem, is separable. We show in the case of gapped ground states in any dimension that the entanglement length is finite on finite subsystems. Restricting to one-dimensional systems, we prove that normal matrix product states have a finite entanglement length independent of $A$ and $C$, and that a finite pure state with such uniform entanglement length has a matrix product state representation with bond dimension independent of $A$ and $C$. Consequently, in one dimension, entanglement length distinguishes matrix product states from all other pure states.
item.dc:creator: Robert Ferydouni, Thomas Jackson, Samuel O. Scalet

item.title: (Sharp arithmetic) localization beyond transversality
item.description: arXiv:2610.17139v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove sharp arithmetic localization for one-dimensional quasiperiodic potentials with jump discontinuities, beyond uniform transversality. Our results include every non-constant $C^1$ monotone sampling function, even with arbitrarily large flat regions, and also certain non-monotone potentials. A key new mechanism is a symbolic unique-continuation principle: first-return words to the region where $f'>0$ have no common Dirichlet resonance, forcing eigenfunction mass to transfer away from flat or negatively sloped regions and recovering quantitative monotonicity of finite-volume eigenvalue branches.
item.dc:creator: Svetlana Jitomirskaya, Netanel Levi, Tom Stoiber

item.title: Global synchronization in time-varying directed higher-order networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.17150v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Global synchronization has been largely investigated in static higher-order networks and little attention has been brought to directed, temporal higher-order networks. We hereby make a step in this direction by studying the emergence of global synchronization in periodically fast switching systems with directed higher-order interactions. By working in the framework of the Master Stability Function, we show that the linearized dynamics includes two time-dependent Jacobian matrices, both evolving on the timescale of the synchronous solution, together with a generalized Laplacian evolving on a fast switching timescale, resulting from the hypergraph time evolution. To address this two-timescale structure, we establish a fast-switching stability criterion for directed balanced higher-order structures. The latter condition allows to decouple the parallel and transverse perturbations to the synchronization manifold. By relying on the average theory for dynamical systems, we are able to prove exponential stability of global synchronization in the fast switching higher-order network. The proposed theory is then illustrated by using a higher-order Stuart--Landau model, which provides a natural benchmark for the theory. Directionality can move Laplacian eigenvalues into instability regions off the real axis, hence destabilizing synchronization; our results nevertheless reveal that temporal switching can counteract this destabilizing effect and restore global synchronization when the directed structures alternate sufficiently rapidly, even though the instantaneous directed higher-order structures are individually unstable.
item.dc:creator: Wilfried Segnou, Timoteo Carletti, Dibakar Ghosh

item.title: Models for dagger $(\infty,1)$-categories III: Univalent flagged dagger $(\infty,1)$-categories and unitarily complete dagger Segal anima
item.description: arXiv:2610.17311v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We identify the $(\infty,1)$-category presented by the dagger Bergner, dagger Joyal, and dagger Rezk models of Parts I and II with that of univalent flagged dagger $(\infty,1)$-categories. We first construct a realization--nerve adjunction between reversal simplicial anima and Hermitian flags. We prove that its nerve restricts to an equivalence between flagged dagger $(\infty,1)$-categories and dagger Segal anima, under which univalence corresponds to unitary completeness. We then construct the adjunctions for univalentization and Hermitian completion and identify univalentization with unitary completion.
item.dc:creator: Keima Akasaka

item.title: Kinetic SDEs and kinetic Fokker-Planck equations with critical Morrey-type drifts, and local blow-ups
item.description: arXiv:2610.17319v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a Sobolev theory for the kinetic Fokker-Planck equation subject to a singular Morrey-form $L^\infty+M^q_K$ force field which can produce local blow-ups due to strong attraction to a submanifold. Our approach is based on the fractional representation for the Duhamel series of the equation and on establishing kinetic Adams-type estimates. Accordingly, we construct weak solutions of Brownian-driven kinetic SDEs in a critical Morrey set-up, obtain kinetic Krylov-type estimates and a strongly continuous Feller propagator, and establish uniqueness criteria for a large class of weak solutions.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Jabir, Damir Kinzebulatov, Chengjun Yue

item.title: Yang-Baxter deformed sigma models on $\mathrm{SU}(N)/\mathrm{SO}(N)$
item.description: arXiv:2610.17362v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study Yang--Baxter deformations of two-dimensional sigma models on compact symmetric spaces $\mathrm{SU}(N)/\mathrm{SO}(N)$, with particular emphasis on their ultraviolet behavior. We claim that the ultraviolet fixed point is described by the $\mathrm{SO}(N,\mathbb C)/\mathrm{SO}(N,\mathbb R)$ non-compact WZW model together with $N-1$ compact free bosons. We determine the leading correction to this fixed point and identify it with the perturbation generated by the corresponding screening currents. We also extend our construction to the broader class of symmetric spaces of maximal rank.
item.dc:creator: Danila Alexandrov, Alexey Bychkov, Ivan Kalinichenko, Alexey Litvinov

item.title: Fresnel scattering for open waveguide networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.17398v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper concerns the Helmholtz scattering problem for open waveguide networks, extending the analysis from [arXiv:2302.04353, arXiv:2310.05816, arXiv:2401.04674] to plane-wave incident data. We first reduce the problem to a Fredholm second-kind integral equation on an infinite interface. This produces an integral representation of the solution to the original scattering problem, which is then used to obtain detailed asymptotic estimates of the solution at infinity. To leading order and away from the waveguides, the scattered field is itself a plane wave. Its amplitude and phase shift exhibit a jump across a critical polar angle depending on the direction of the incident plane-wave. Our estimates also imply that the scattered field is outgoing in a weak sense, allowing us to establish a uniqueness result. We conclude by calculating the waveguide-mode contributions to the scattered field in a perturbative regime.
item.dc:creator: Solomon Quinn, Charles L. Epstein

item.title: Schauder estimate in large scale for compressible planar cavity flows with fast-decaying vorticity
item.description: arXiv:2610.17522v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we study planar compressible cavity flows fast-decaying vorticity and establish a Schauder estimate in large scale. As an application, we obtain an a priori asymptotic growth rate estimate of the cavity, that $s^{\frac{1}{2}-\delta}\lesssim h(s)\lesssim s^{\frac{1}{2}+\delta}$. This is by far the most accurate asymptotic estimate for compressible cavity flows and is probably the first paper that takes vorticity into account in the asymptotic analysis.
item.dc:creator: Chilin Zhang

item.title: On quasi-lisse affine vertex algebras $L_{-1-h/6}(\mathfrak{g})$ from rank-one Argyres-Douglas theories
item.description: arXiv:2610.17676v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study certain simple affine vertex algebras $L_{-1-h/6}(\mathfrak{g})$ from rank-one Argyres-Douglas theories, where $\mathfrak{g}$ is a non-simply-laced simple Lie algebra and $h$ is its Coxeter number. For $L_{-3}(F_4)$, we determine the maximal ideal of $V^{-3}(F_4)$, Zhu's algebra, and the associated variety. We also classify the irreducible highest-weight $L_{-3}(F_4)$-modules and determine the characters of its irreducible ordinary modules. The associated variety is $\overline{\mathbb{O}}_{\widetilde A_1}$, and the level $-3$ is totally collapsing for the orbit $\mathbb{O}_{\widetilde A_1}$. The Poisson coinvariants of the $C_2$-algebra of $L_{-3}(F_4)$ are isomorphic to $\mathbb{C}[\ell]/(\ell^5)$, where $\ell$ is induced by the conformal vector. Consequently, the characters of ordinary $L_{-3}(F_4)$-modules satisfy a fifth-order modular linear differential equation. We also give modular linear differential equations of orders five and eleven satisfied by the characters of ordinary modules for $L_{-2}(B_3)$ and $L_{-2}(G_2)$ respectively.
item.dc:creator: Drazen Adamovic, Xuanzhong Dai, Kaiwen Sun

item.title: Yau's number-theoretic conjecture and sharp spectral bounds for quantum harmonic oscillators
item.description: arXiv:2610.17704v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove Yau's number-theoretic conjecture on positive integral points in real right simplices in every dimension $n\ge3$, and apply the resulting sharp polynomial bound to quantum harmonic oscillators. The lattice-point bound holds for every choice of positive real intercepts for which the count is nonzero, with equality precisely when all intercepts equal the same integer. For oscillators in dimensions $n\ge3$, we obtain explicit upper bounds for eigenvalue counts and spectral remainders for arbitrary positive frequencies at every threshold at or above the lowest eigenvalue. For frequencies with rational ratios in dimensions $n\ge2$, an additional lattice coordinate and interpolation give bounds for energy sums, or first Riesz means, at every threshold. When all frequencies are equal (the isotropic case), the oscillator attains these bounds: the counting bound is exact at its energy levels, and interpolation on its natural energy grid recovers the energy sum at every threshold. In three dimensions, the exact formula displays the periodic contribution associated with the resonance discussed by Fefferman and Seco. The proof builds on the slicing method of Yau and Zhang. Arithmetic and geometric consequences include explicit bounds for smooth numbers and lattice-point discrepancies.
item.dc:creator: Zhiwen Liu, Stephen S. -T. Yau, Hao Zuo

item.title: Sampling from the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Model up to Criticality
item.description: arXiv:2610.17717v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the simulated annealing algorithm efficiently samples from the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model at inverse temperature $\beta < 1$ to an arbitrary inverse polynomial accuracy in total variation.
item.dc:creator: Hang Du, Brice Huang, Sidhanth Mohanty, Amit Rajaraman

item.title: Beyond the circle: current algebras, geometry and higher gauge structures
item.description: arXiv:2610.17781v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Replacing the circle by a manifold leads to current Lie algebras and their central and derivation extensions. We separate the coefficient algebra, harmonic analysis and geometric data. Differentials modulo exact forms describe central extensions; divergence-free vector fields give explicit cocycles, whose compatible derivations satisfy a stabilizer equation. Compact examples include the three-sphere and its current--Virasoro extension. We also explain the analytic qualifications for SL(2,R) and its symmetric space and the role of transported multiplication in soft geometries. The recent harmonic constructions of Campoamor-Stursberg, Marrani and Rausch de Traubenberg are compared with the cohomological work of Coquereaux, Frappat, Ragoucy and Sorba and Castellani's loop geometry and infinite-dimensional free differential algebras. A coefficient-algebra construction connects currents to higher brackets and clarifies the additional requirements of a dynamical theory. For Lie algebras of order F, central extensions obey coupled binary and symmetric F-ary conditions, with explicit examples and obstructions.
item.dc:creator: R. Campoamor-Stursberg, A. Marrani, M. Rausch de Traubenberg

item.title: Classical and quantum scattering of massive Klein--Gordon fields in asymptotically flat spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2610.17819v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We use microlocal tools to define distinguished incoming and outgoing vacuum states of the quantum theory of massive Klein--Gordon fields in non-trapping asymptotically flat spacetimes, including radiative perturbations of Minkowski space. The asymptotic vacuum states satisfy the Hadamard condition, and the incoming and outgoing particle representations are unitarily equivalent, or in other words the quantum S-matrix is well-defined. These results are based on a description of scattering of classical fields which keeps track of the asymptotic distinction between positive- and negative-frequency solutions of the Klein--Gordon equation. Our emphasis is on developing the theory without recourse to explicit asymptotics for classical waves.
item.dc:creator: Mikhail Molodyk

item.title: Metaplectic-c prequantizations and the Einstein--Brillouin--Keller quantizability condition
item.description: arXiv:2610.17890v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that every symplectic manifold admits a symplectic form whose metaplectic-c prequantizations give quantizability conditions on all its Lagrangian submanifolds. Metaplectic-c prequantizations descend to prequantizations over the Lagrangian Grassmannian bundle that are fibrewise flat with holonomies primitive fourth roots of unity on the generators of the fundamental groups. This fibrewise holonomy is consistently interpreted as that of both Leray two-orientations and normalized Blattner--Kostant--Sternberg half-forms. The prequantizations pull back to flat circle bundles on each Lagrangian submanifold whose holonomy character defines a quantizability condition. The first and second Stiefel--Whitney classes are identified as splitting obstructions to the Lagrangianwise holonomies. These holonomies split into a product of holonomies on any orientable Lagrangian submanifold, and split consistently for all Lagrangian submanifolds of a manifold with metaplectic structure. When the first Chern class vanishes, the holonomy splits into the Bohr--Sommerfeld factor and a quarter phase Maslov correction, recovering the classical Einstein--Brillouin--Keller condition. We develop the underlying obstruction theory for circle extensions associated to general Lie group double coverings with first hypercohomology groupoids.
item.dc:creator: Hyunmoon Kim

item.title: Cubic Nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger Systems and Orthonormal Fermionic Ground States in $\mathbb R$
item.description: arXiv:2610.17941v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the one-dimensional nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger system \[ -u_i''-2\Big(\sum_{k=1}^N u_k^2\Big)^{p-1}u_i=\mu_i u_i \quad \mbox{in } \ \mathbb R,\ \ i=1,2,\cdots,N, \tag{S} \] where $u=(u_1,\cdots,u_N)\in H^1(\mathbb{R})^N$, $\mu_1\leq\mu_2\leq\cdots\leq\mu_N<0$, $1<p<3$ and $N\geq 2$ are arbitrary. For the cubic case where $p=2$ and $N\ge 2$, we establish the following structural results of the system $(S)$: (i) all nontrivial solutions can be classified completely; (ii) the linearized operator at any nontrivial solution is non-degenerate; (iii) exact $L^2$-mass formulas of all nontrivial solutions are derived in terms of distinct Lagrange multipliers $\mu_i$. As the applications of the above structural results, we first show that the system $(S)$ with $p=2$ does not have any orthonormal solution for any $N\ge2$. We then investigate a fermionic variational problem $J_N(p)$ with $N\ge2$, whose minimizers correspond to ground states of the system $(S)$ under orthonormal constraints. More precisely, we prove that there exists a sufficiently small $\delta_N>0$ such that $J_N(p)$ is attained for any $p\in(2-\delta_N,2)$, whereas $J_N(p)$ is not attained for any $p\in[2,2+\delta_N)$. These settle some conjectures of [Gontier--Lewin--Nazar, ARMA, 2021] and [Frank--Gontier--Lewin, CMP, 2021].
item.dc:creator: Bin Chen, Yujin Guo, Yong Luo, Juncheng Wei

item.title: The Brownian bubble tea
item.description: arXiv:2610.17990v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We use Loewner-Kufarev evolution to decompose the Brownian loop soup into a Poisson point process on Brownian bubbles which we call the Brownian bubble tea driven by $\rho$, where $\rho$ is the driving measure for the Loewner chain. The only assumption on $\rho$ is that the evolving boundaries are locally connected. This generalizes a similar disintegration result of Lawler and Werner to essentially optimal regularity, and includes foliations with finite Loewner-Kufarev energy as well as radial and whole-plane $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa$ for all $\kappa \geqslant 0$. As applications, we give Brownian loop interpretations of the conformal distortion formula for Loewner-Kufarev energy and the relationships between the Loewner energy, Loewner-Kufarev energy, and the Schwarzian action.
item.dc:creator: Gregory F. Lawler, Fredrik Viklund, Yilin Wang, Catherine Wolfram

item.title: Eigenvalue fluctuations for the crushed ice problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.18013v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the eigenvalues of the negative Dirichlet Laplacian $-\Delta$ in domain $D_{\epsilon,N}$ obtained by removing $N$ Euclidean balls of radius $\epsilon$ from a bounded open set $D\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ ($d\ge2$). It is known that, for the balls centered at points drawn independently from a distribution with probability density $\rho$ and for $N\to\infty$ and $\epsilon\downarrow0$ so that the aggregate Newtonian capacity of the removed balls tends to some $\kappa>0$, the eigenvalues of $-\Delta$ in $D_{\epsilon,N}$ homogenize to those of the Schr\"odinger operator $-\Delta+\kappa\rho$ in $D$. Here we prove that, for the eigenvalues that are simple in the limit, a multivariate Central Limit Theorem holds in all $d\ge2$ under centering by expected values. Unlike earlier work in $d=3$ by Figari, Orlandi and Teta and, independently, Ozawa from 1980s that was based on resolvent expansions, we rely on martingale representations and one-ball perturbation asymptotic controlled by methods of harmonic analysis.
item.dc:creator: Marek Biskup, Ryoki Fukushima

item.title: Optimization Inverse Spectral Problem for the Schr\"odinger Operator on a Compact Graph
item.description: arXiv:2610.18081v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the optimization inverse spectral problem (OISP) for the first $m$ eigenvalues of the Schr\"odinger operator on a compact metric graph. We prove the existence of a solution for every strictly increasing finite set of prescribed eigenvalues. On a graph without cycles, we obtain a representation of the optimal correction as a linear combination of squared eigenfunctions, provided that the selected eigenvalues are simple and separated from the next eigenvalue. On a graph with cycles, under the same simplicity and separation assumptions, we obtain a strong limiting representation of the optimal potential in terms of eigenfunctions of approximating operators. For a graph with a cycle, we give a counterexample with simple eigenvalues and linearly dependent squared eigenfunctions. We also prove that linear dependence of the squares of nonzero restrictions to an edge of eigenfunctions corresponding to distinct eigenvalues forces the potential on that edge to have an analytic representative
item.dc:creator: Valeev Nur

item.title: Supersymmetric Observables from Surface Defect Anomalies in 4d and 6d SCFTs
item.description: arXiv:2610.18086v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the contributions of half-BPS surface defects to supersymmetric Casimir energy and the universal logarithmic term of supersymmetric R\'enyi entropy in four- and six-dimensional SCFTs. Using equivariant integration of defect anomaly polynomials and its extension to supersymmetric R\'enyi backgrounds, we obtain closed expressions for these observables in terms of defect 't Hooft anomalies. For Gukov--Witten defects preserving transverse rotations in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N} = 4$ super Yang--Mills theories, both observables depend on a single R-symmetry anomaly. For $\mathcal{N} = (0, 4)$ defects in six-dimensional $\mathcal{N} = (1, 0)$ theories, additional terms arise from the gravitational anomaly. We provide complementary checks using chiral algebras, five-dimensional localization, and holographic probe branes at large $N$, while localized chiral fermions reproduce the gravitational-anomaly contributions. The framework also recovers Wilson-surface results in six-dimensional $\mathcal{N} = (2, 0)$ theories.
item.dc:creator: Zi-Xiao Huang, Ma-Ke Yuan, Yang Zhou

item.title: Large deviations, gradient flows and fluctuating hydrodynamics for fractional diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2610.18182v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This work is a step towards a general understanding of fluctuations for systems of particles described at large scale by fractional diffusion. First, we derive formally a Large Deviation Principle for the empirical measure of mean-field interacting particles with a L{\'e}vy-type noise. In the case of independent particles, this unveils a generalized gradient flow structure at large scales. Second, we derive and solve numerically a stochastic Partial Differential Equation describing the fluctuating hydrodynamics of this system. The results compare well with direct numerical integration of the particles' dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Julien Barre (IDP), Hiroshi Horii

item.title: Square-Root Profiles and Sharp Fourier Decay of Quasiperiodic Spectral Measures
item.description: arXiv:2610.18259v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study spectral measures of one-dimensional quasiperiodic Schr\"odinger operators. For subcritical Schr\"odinger operator with Diophantine frequency, we prove sharp measurable-set bounds, answering a question of Avila and Jitomirskaya \cite{AJ}; we prove optimal Fourier decay and the sharp decay order of the time-averaged quantum return probability, confirming a conjecture of Aloisio, Carvalho, and de Oliveira \cite{ACO} and a prediction of Zhong and Mosseri \cite{ZhongMosseri}. For the subcritical almost Mathieu operator, we establish summable square-root envelopes for the spectral density, with an optimal density-one formulation of the lower bound, thereby answering a question of Avila \cite{Aqi}. These results follow from a general theorem for reflectionless measures under a summable square-root Craig-type condition. We establish an exact residue expansion of the squared Borel transform, which connects local density blow-up with long-time averaged return probabilities: the endpoint residues determine both the square-root edge profiles and the leading coefficient of the time-averaged return probability.
item.dc:creator: Zhenfu Wang, Qi Zhou

item.title: Beyond Gaussian Entanglement: Practical Criteria for Polynomially Excited Quantum States
item.description: arXiv:2610.18365v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Polynomial excitations consisting of creation and annihilation operators are studied. Subsystem entanglement is proven produced and preserved by such manipulations. NPT entanglement already present between any two subsystems of a general pure or mixed multipartite Gaussian state is preserved under all polynomial excitations. Nevertheless, these excitations can create NPT entanglement between initially separable subsystems, implying that the number of NPT entangled pairs cannot decrease. Polynomial excitations of a wide class of initially separable pure states are considered. For these states, the method reduces the infinite-dimensional positivity problem to a finite-dimensional one: after partial transposition, NPT entanglement is equivalent to a corresponding bilinear representation matrix not being positive semi-definite. Furthermore, using symplectic diagonalization and spectral decomposition, an explicit transformation is constructed between the Fock-space and position representations. It is applied to quadratic excitations of a three-mode mixed Gaussian state. The behavior of the NPT entanglement is tracked between subsystems as a function of a parameter $\kappa$, which tunes the non-locality of the excitation, and quantum negativity is evaluated. Under a chosen quadratic Hamiltonian, the resulting unitary time evolution maintains NPT entanglement for long intervals, interrupted only by short periods of PPT states. Finally, a closed analytical expression is derived for the covariance matrix of a general quadratic operator for an arbitrary number of degrees of freedom in phase space. Our framework directly connects mathematical foundations, theoretical modeling, and experimentally feasible implementations.
item.dc:creator: G\'abor Homa, Rich\'ard Balka, Nikolett N\'emet, Andr\'as Bodor, Tam\'as Kiss, Andr\'as Csord\'as

item.title: Stability of the Markov-Krein Transform Under Classical Convolutions
item.description: arXiv:2610.18436v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that, for every $c>0$, the image of the generalized Markov-Krein transform on probability measures with finite logarithmic moment is closed under classical additive convolution and under the Mellin convolution. This resolves the positivity conjecture for the additive high-temperature convolution, a one-parameter interpolation between classical and free convolution arising in random matrix theory and representation theory in the regime $N\to\infty, N\beta_N/2\to c$. Our proof relies on a convolution theorem for universally prestarlike functions.
item.dc:creator: Pierre Mergny

item.title: A Central Limit Theorem for High-Temperature SYK Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.18440v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev (SYK) model is a quantum many-body model of Majorana fermions with all-to-all random interactions. It has attracted wide interest in condensed matter and high-energy physics as a solvable model of non-Fermi liquids and holography. Fix an even integer $q\geq4$, and let $Z_N(\beta)$ be the partition function of the Gaussian $q$-body SYK model. We prove that for all sufficiently small inverse temperatures $\beta > 0$, there exists $\rho=\rho(\beta)>0$ such that \[ N^{q/2 -1}(\log Z_N(\beta)-\mathbb{E}[\log Z_N(\beta)]) \Longrightarrow \mathcal{N}(0,\rho^2). \] In addition to the mathematical results, we discuss how the proofs were developed and refined through interaction between human researchers and AI, and we describe the subsequent formalization of the main arguments in Lean 4. This work thus serves as a case study of a research workflow that integrates human insight, AI-assisted exploration, iterative proof refinement, and formal verification.
item.dc:creator: Yoshinori Kamijima, Shuta Nakajima, Ryoichiro Noda, K\^{o}hei Sasaya

item.title: Sign-indefinite transmission conditions and near-zero eigenvalues and resonances
item.description: arXiv:2610.18483v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the linear operator for metamaterial modeling $$L_{c,d }=(\chi_{\RE^{3}\backslash\overline \Omega}+c)\nabla\!\cdot (\chi_{\RE^{3}\backslash\overline \Omega}+d)\nabla\,,$$ where the material parameters $c>0$ and $d$ are constant on each connected component of the bounded domain $\Omega$, $d$ is negative on at least one component of $\Omega$ and transmission boundary conditions hold at the interfaces. It turns out that $L_{c,d }$ has, as in the sign-definite case, an absolutely continuous spectrum equal to $[0,+\infty)$; however, contrary to the latter, it has a non-empty point spectrum; in particular, we find conditions on the parameters so that zero is a threshold eigenvalue. In the case $\Omega$ is connected, we study how such a threshold eigenvalue behaves under $\varepsilon$-small analytic perturbations of the parameters. We show that, depending on the position of the number $\frac12\,\frac{1+d(\ve)}{1-d(\ve)}$ relative to the nearest eigenvalue of the Neumann-Poincar\'e operator of the interface, the zero eigenvalue splits into two branches (analytic in $\varepsilon^{1/2}$), consisting either of two branches of resonances, or of one branch of negative eigenvalues and one of resonances.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Mantile, Andrea Posilicano

item.title: Hypergeometric solutions to coupled Klein-Gordon equations in cosmology with small-field excursions
item.description: arXiv:2610.18586v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Klein-Gordon equation is a second order differential equation that appears in a variety of applications in mathematics, physics and engineering. This equation is often solved using numerical methods, since a general analytical solution is unattainable. However, one can find very useful analytical solutions for some special cases. In cosmology, the Klein-Gordon equation of a field can explain the physics of inflation and has important consequences on understanding the origin and evolution of the universe. An analytical solution to the Klein-Gordon equation in cosmology has been obtained in the small-field excursion approximation, and it turns out that the solution can be written in terms of the confluent hypergeometric limit function. In this work, we derive this result again while showing the details of the calculations and then generalize to the case of two coupled Klein-Gordon equations. We show that the solution of this coupled system can be written in terms of Kummer's hypergeometric limit function while considering minimal assumptions. We carry out a full numerical calculation of the coupled system and compare it to the results from the analytical expressions.
item.dc:creator: Amin Aboubrahim, Anastasiia Minenkova, Tomas Yonkers

item.title: A proof of the framed LMOV conjecture for links
item.description: arXiv:2610.18618v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the Labastida--Mari\~no--Ooguri--Vafa conjecture for oriented links with arbitrary integer framings. Consequently, the framed reformulated invariants have finite integral LMOV expansions for every integer framing vector.
item.dc:creator: Kefeng Liu, Pan Peng, Shengmao Zhu

item.title: A three-block higher-rank deformed Hermitian--Yang--Mills correspondence on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$
item.description: arXiv:2610.18788v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the invariant rank-four deformed Hermitian--Yang--Mills equation associated with the chain $\mathcal{O}(1)\to\mathcal{O}(2)^{\oplus2}\to\mathcal{O}(3)$ over $\mathbb P^1$, with vertical weights $(4,2,0)$ and a fixed product K\"ahler class and phase. For arbitrary linear arrows $\psi=Bz$ and $\phi=(Az)^T$, smooth strictly calibrated reduced solutions exist exactly when $A$ is invertible and $z^TA^TBz$ is not identically zero. The same condition characterizes stability, semistability and polystability in the specified equivariant coherent category. The classification includes all eleven nonempty coefficient strata and both coincident and distinct divisor points on the rank-one lower boundary. The analytic proof retains the ordered, noncommuting middle equation. After constructing positive-parameter solutions, it rules out unbounded metric values by combining the source budgets with moving spectral tests; on the rank-one lower boundary, the divisor mass must also be retained. Global value, gradient and symbol estimates then give a smooth strictly calibrated endpoint on the original chain. No equivalence with full coherent or derived-category stability, uniqueness, or estimate uniform across changing chains is asserted.
item.dc:creator: Yuqi Li, Hao-Yu Sun

item.title: Cellular Algebra of $A_2$ webs
item.description: arXiv:2610.18801v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a diagram algebra $\mathcal{K}_L$ based on Kuperberg's $A_2$-webs and prove a Schur--Weyl duality $\mathcal{K}_L \cong \operatorname{End}_{U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3)}((V^+ \oplus V^-)^{\otimes L})$, where $V^\pm$ are the fundamental representations of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$. Thus, $\mathcal{K}_L$ is a natural $A_2$ analogue of the Temperley--Lieb algebra. We construct an explicit cellular structure for $\mathcal{K}_L$, with the web basis as its cellular basis and cell modules indexed by dominant $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$-weights. The bases of these modules are parametrized by dominant lattice paths via a recursive growth algorithm. Using this structure, we determine local generators of $\mathcal{K}_L$ and establish web formulations of the first and second fundamental theorems of invariant theory. In particular, we show that the braid-group image, augmented by local idempotents, does not generate $\mathcal{K}_L$, and identify an additional local generator. Finally, we derive a bimodule decomposition of $(V^+ \oplus V^-)^{\otimes L}$, yielding a complete set of irreducible $\mathcal{K}_L$-modules for formal or generic $q$.
item.dc:creator: Azat M. Gainutdinov, Jesper Lykke Jacobsen, Yueheng Li

item.title: On the coincidence of discrete and continuous definitions of Entanglement of Formation
item.description: arXiv:2610.18816v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: It is proved that every Borel ensemble of pure states on a separable bipartite Hilbert space with finite average entanglement admits a countable ensemble with the same barycenter and arbitrarily small additional average entanglement. Consequently, the discrete and continuous versions of the Entanglement of Formation coincide on the whole space of states of infinite-dimensional bipartite quantum system (with infinite values allowed). The main idea of the proof (realized with the AI-assistance) is the identification of a Borel ensemble of pure bipartite states with a Borel probability measure on the unit sphere of the space of Hilbert--Schmidt operators followed by dividing the support of this measure into appropriate cells and replacing each cell by its conditional barycenter. The resulting countable ensemble is obtained by a recursive construction.
item.dc:creator: Haobo Ma, Maksim E. Shirokov, Wenlin Zhang

item.title: Superdiffusive Invariance Principle for the two-dimensional Asymmetric Simple Exclusion Process
item.description: arXiv:2610.18847v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the Asymmetric Simple Exclusion Process (ASEP) at its critical dimension $d=2$, started from the Bernoulli product measure with density $\rho \in (0,1)$. We first derive the sharp $\log(t)^{2/3}$ divergence of the bulk diffusivity, predicted via mode-coupling theory in [H. van Beijeren, R. Kutner, H. Spohn, Phys. Rev. Lett., 1985], including the exact prefactor, thereby removing the subleading diverging multiplicative corrections in the Tauberian bounds of [H.-T. Yau, Ann. of Math., 2004]. More importantly, we establish an invariance principle for the density fluctuation field on the corresponding superdiffusive scales. On the time scale $\tau$, we rescale space by $\sqrt{\tau} \log(\tau)^{1/3}$ in the direction of the drift and by $\sqrt{\tau}$ in the transverse direction, and prove functional convergence of the rescaled fluctuation process to the solution of a conservative stochastic heat equation with additive noise. This is the same explicit Gaussian Fixed Point obtained in [G. Cannizzaro, Q. Moulard, F. Toninelli, arXiv:2501.00344, 2025] for the two-dimensional Stochastic Burgers Equation (SBE). We also deduce a superdiffusive central limit theorem for the second-class particle under the same anisotropic rescaling. The result holds for any finite-range jump kernel with nonzero drift and uniaxial asymmetry. This is the first space-time scaling limit result for a nonequilibrium interacting particle system at the critical dimension, where Gaussian fluctuations emerge despite logarithmic corrections to the scaling. The proof uses an approximate fluctuation-dissipation relation, which is obtained by combining a sharp quantitative comparison between the ASEP and SBE generators with refined estimates on the SBE Ansatz. An additional key novelty is a tightness argument that overcomes the limitations of the It\^o trick on superdiffusive scales.
item.dc:creator: Quentin Moulard

item.title: Regularized interacting scalar quantum field theories
item.description: arXiv:2502.14117v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we consider self-interacting scalar quantum field theories over a $d$-dimensional Minkowski spacetime with various interaction Lagrangians which are suitable functions of the field. The interacting field observables are represented as power series over the free theory by means of perturbation theory. The object which is employed to obtain this power series is the time-ordered exponential of the interaction Lagrangian which is the $S$-matrix of the theory and thus itself a power series in the coupling constant of the theory. We analyze a regularization procedure which makes the $S$-matrix convergent to well-defined unitary operators. This regularization depends on two parameters. One describes how much the high-frequency contributions in the propagators are tamed and a second one describes how much the large-field contributions are suppressed in the interaction Lagrangian. We finally discuss the limits in which the parameters are removed in some lower-dimensional theories and for specific interaction Lagrangians. In particular, we show, by an abstract argument, that in three spacetime dimensions for a $\phi^4_3$ theory one obtains sequences of unitary operators which are weakly-$*$ convergent to bounded operators in the limit of vanishing parameters. Although we lose control over the unitarity of the operator obtained in the limit and although the uniqueness of the limit is not under control, we notice that some basic causal properties are satisfied by the corresponding interacting fields. We furthermore observe that the very same limits, applied at fixed order, give back the ordinary perturbation theory results. Finally, we discuss a possible extension of these results to the case of a $\phi^4_4$ theory.
item.dc:creator: Nicola Pinamonti

item.title: Partition functions of two-dimensional Coulomb gases with circular root- and jump-type singularities
item.description: arXiv:2510.00843v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study the random polynomial $p_n(\rho):=\prod_{j=1}^n (|z_j|-\rho)$, where the points $\{z_j\}_{j=1}^n$ are the eigenvalue moduli of random normal matrices with a radially symmetric potential. We establish precise large $n$ asymptotic expansions for the moment generating function \[ \mathbb{E}\!\left[e^{\tfrac{u}{\pi}\mathrm{Im}\log p_n(\rho)}\, e^{a\,\mathrm{Re}\log p_n(\rho)}\right], \qquad u\in\mathbb{R}, \; a>-1, \] where $\rho>0$ lies in the bulk of the spectral droplet. The asymptotic expansion is expressed in terms of parabolic cylinder functions, which confirms a conjecture of Byun and Charlier. This also provides the first free energy expansion of two-dimensional Coulomb gases with general circular root- and jump-type singularities. While the $a=0$ case has already been widely studied in the literature due to its relation to counting statistics, we also obtain new results for this special case.
item.dc:creator: Kohei Noda

item.title: Wave scattering by a transversal defect in a discrete waveguide
item.description: arXiv:2602.10227v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study wave scattering by a finite transversal strip in a discrete square-lattice waveguide with Dirichlet boundary conditions imposed on the strip and the waveguide walls. The setting is motivated as a discrete analogue of the classical continuous waveguide problem with a screen. The corresponding Wiener--Hopf formulation leads to an equation with a $4 \times 4$ matrix kernel, which reduces to a $2 \times 2$ matrix kernel under some symmetry assumptions. The prospects for factorising this kernel are discussed, but this approach is not pursued. Instead, an exact analytical solution is obtained using the pole removal technique. This contrasts with the continuous case, where only approximate solutions are currently available. The reflection and transmission coefficients resulting from an incident duct mode are computed with an accuracy up to $10^{-13}$, showing consistency with theoretical predictions from continuous waveguide theory. In particular, full reflection and zero transmission are recovered as the frequency approaches the cut-off value for the incident mode. Finally, the solution is validated against a numerical computation of the diffraction problem via the Boundary Algebraic Equations method with a tailored lattice Green's function.
item.dc:creator: Elena Medvedeva, Raphael Assier, Anastasia Kisil

item.title: Deformed and undeformed localized wave solutions for the two-component (2+1)-dimensional Fokas-Lenells equation
item.description: arXiv:2604.23684v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we focus on the two-component (2+1)-dimensional Fokas-Lenells equation, which models the propagation of ultrashort optical pulses in nonlinear media with multi-mode interactions and multi-dimensional effects. Firstly, we construct the determinant form of the generalized Darboux transformation (DT). Secondly, we obtain deformed solitons, deformed positons on the zero background and deformed breathers, deformed Y-shaped breathers on the nonzero backgrounds by DT method. Finally, the undeformed solutions including higher-order rogue wave solutions and breather-rogue wave solutions are derived by generalized DT. This work enriches the solution family associated with the equation, but also illustrates the efficiency of DT method in multi-dimensional and multi-component systems.
item.dc:creator: Yanan Wang, Minghe Zhang

item.title: Affine Left--Right Dirac Data on the Moyal Plane, with an Application to $U(1)_\star$ Gauge Coupling in Noncommutative Quantum Mechanics
item.description:
arXiv:2605.10250v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study even non-unital Dirac data on the two-dimensional Moyal plane with fixed deformation parameter \(\vartheta
eq0\), whose Dirac operator is affine in the left and right regular coordinate multipliers, with coefficient matrices \(T_L\) and \(T_R\). Two invariants organize this class. The right block controls algebra--Dirac transversality: local compactness holds if and only if \(\det T_R
eq0\), with \(|\det T_R|\) determining the local volume coefficient and \(\operatorname{sgn}\det T_R\) the oriented Gaussian \(K\)-homology pairing. Independently, \(\Gamma=\vartheta(\det T_L-\det T_R)\) controls the spectral regime and, together with \(|\det T_R|\), the exact localized heat trace: \(\Gamma
eq0\) gives infinitely degenerate Landau levels, while for \(\Gamma=0\) in the transverse regime the spectrum is \(\mathbb R\) with empty point spectrum. Applied to Wallet's Landau--Moyal family, the criterion shows that local compactness survives at the metric-degenerate point \(\xi_{\mathrm W}=1\) but fails at \(\xi_{\mathrm W}=-1\), thereby resolving the local-compactness behaviour at both exceptional one-sided points. We then derive a distinguished affine family from a fixed nondegenerate sector \((\hbar_0,\vartheta_0,B_0)\) of the kinematical symmetry group of two-dimensional noncommutative quantum mechanics. The sector fixes the effective Moyal scale \(\vartheta_{\mathrm{eff}}=\vartheta_0/(1-\vartheta_0B_0/\hbar_0)\) and \(T_R\), while an affine \(U(1)_\star\) background coupling deforms only the left affine part of the Dirac operator. Consequently, local compactness, noncommutative volume and \(K\)-homology class remain unchanged, whereas \(\Gamma=	frac12(1-eF_{xy}/B_0)\) drives a transition at \(eF_{xy}=B_0\) from Landau levels to spectrum \(\mathbb R\) with empty point spectrum.
item.dc:creator: Tanmoy Kumar Sarkar, Md. Rafsanjany Jim, S. Hasibul Hassan Chowdhury

item.title: The massless sine-Gordon model with logarithmic correlations in arbitrary dimension
item.description: arXiv:2606.06657v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we study the sine-Gordon model with logarithmic correlations in arbitrary dimension $d \ge 1$. The model is defined as a Euclidean field theory whose interaction term in the classical action is \[ S_{\mathrm{int}}(\varphi) := 2z \int_{\Lambda} \cos(\sqrt{\beta}\,\varphi)\,\dx, \] where $\varphi$ is a logarithmically correlated Gaussian field on a compact domain $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ that coincides with the Gaussian free field when $d=2$, and where $z \in \mathbb{R}$ and $\beta>0$. We treat both the massive and massless cases, with the main emphasis on the massless regime. We construct the field without imposing boundary conditions, together with its charge and gradient correlation functions, and we show that the partition function is renormalizable. The results are non-perturbative, holding for all $z \in \mathbb{R}$. If $d=1$, our results are valid for the full subcritical range $\beta\in (0,4\pi)$ and if $d\geq 2$, the results are valid for $\beta\in (0,(d+1)2\pi)$. Our analysis is carried out directly in the continuum: we perform renormalization via a scale decomposition and control the partition function by controlling the renormalized potential that arises in this procedure, using the iterated Mayer expansion of Brydges and Kennedy~\cite{BrKe87a}.
item.dc:creator: Sami Vihko

item.title: Heat Kernel and Resurgence
item.description: arXiv:2606.21909v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the resurgent structure of short--time heat kernel asymptotics from the viewpoint of Picard--Lefschetz theory. For a real analytic Riemannian manifold, we show the heat kernel admits a 1-- Gevrey small--time expansion whose Borel transform detects complex--geometric data beyond the real geodesic sector. We formulate an infinite--dimensional Picard--Lefschetz problem of Morse--Floer type for the holomorphic energy functional on the complexified path space, and propose a heat--kernel analogue of the Picard--Lefschetz/Alien correspondence. In this framework, pointed alien operators acting on the asymptotic expansion associated with the real geodesic are predicted to produce the formal heat--kernel sectors associated with other holomorphic geodesics, with coefficients given by signed counts of connecting trajectories of the Morse flow. We perform a confirming test of this proposal on the hyperbolic plane $\mathbb{H}_{\R}^2$.
item.dc:creator: Si Li, Yong Li, Xinxing Tang

item.title: Cantor Spectrum via a Reducibility-Duality Bridge for the Mosaic Almost Mathieu Operator
item.description: arXiv:2606.23422v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the mosaic Almost Mathieu operator, a quasiperiodic model that naturally admits a singular strip-Jacobi representation. By establishing a duality framework and extending the correspondence between the integrated density of states and the fibered rotation number to this setting, we obtain an effective reduction to $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ cocycles. As a consequence, combining Aubry duality, reducibility theory, and the Moser--P\"oschel argument, we prove that the spectrum is a Cantor set for all noncritical parameters.
item.dc:creator: Jiawei He, Yuan Shan, Yongjian Wang

item.title: Integration against POVMs in von Neumann algebras and Operational Quantum Reference Frames
item.description: arXiv:2606.27366v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct integrals of uniformly bounded ultraweakly measurable functions against positive operator-valued measures (POVMs) in von Neumann algebras, assuming that the integrand algebra has separable predual. The integral lies in the spatial tensor product and is uniquely characterized by its evaluations on product normal states. Integration is unital and completely positive and descends faithfully to the quotient by POVM-null functions. When both preduals are separable, this quotient is a von Neumann algebra and integration is normal, agreeing with the amplification of scalar POVM integration. We establish a dilation factorization, a Leibniz rule and a Fubini theorem, and specify the additional joint-normality hypothesis needed for realization in an ambient algebra. As an application, under the stated separability and joint-normality assumptions, we extend operational quantum reference frame relativization to covariant POVMs on arbitrary measurable spaces carrying a group action. Its domain is the fixed-point von Neumann algebra of system-valued functions modulo null equality. For homogeneous spaces of second countable locally compact Hausdorff groups with closed stabilizers, this domain is identified with the stabilizer-fixed system algebra. For sharp frames, relativization is a normal unital $*$-homomorphism, faithful when ambient multiplication is injective. For localizable frames on metrizable spaces, restriction recovers continuous integrands at supported configurations. On trivial principal bundles, the domain is identified with system-valued fields on the base. These results provide integration machinery for forthcoming applications to relativistic gauge theories.
item.dc:creator: Jan G{\l}owacki, Yui Kuramochi

item.title: The Lee-Yang property of the Blume-Capel model
item.description: arXiv:2607.16958v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Lee-Yang theory is based on the theorem concerning a property of the ferromagnetic Ising model partition function proved by T. D. Lee and C. N. Yang in 1952. It provides powerful tools for understanding the very nature of phase transitions and critical phenomena in various spin and similar models. Sometimes, this theory is applied to models for which the theorem's validity has not been proved. By the main result of E. H. Lieb and A. D. Sokal, Commun. Math. Phys. 80, 153 (1981), for a given ferromagnetic model, this validity is guaranteed by the same property of the single-spin partition function. Due to the anisotropy term $\sum_i \Delta S_i^2$, the single-spin partition function of the Blume-Capel model fails to have the Lee-Yang property for $\beta \Delta> \ln 2$. In this article, we show that the ferromagnetic interaction in such a model can induce the Lee-Yang property, even for these values of $\beta \Delta$. To the best of our knowledge, it is the first result of this kind.
item.dc:creator: Yuri Kozitsky, Yurij Holovatch

item.title: Stochastic stability of master--slave synchronization for a class of PDEs with Burgers-type nonlinearity
item.description: arXiv:2607.17002v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the stochastic stability of master--slave synchronization for a class of nonlinear evolution equations sharing a Burgers-type convective nonlinearity and a polynomial linear differential operator, including the Burgers, Kuramoto--Sivashinsky, Kawahara, Benney--Lin, and Nikolaevskiy equations. Under periodic boundary conditions, each equation is represented through a Fourier truncation of order $K$, yielding a real state of one-sided complex Fourier coefficients, which is coupled to a slave system driven by observed master data. We first establish local exponential stability of the deterministic zero-error synchronization solution under a simple condition on the coupling strength in the slave model. We then introduce observational noise in the coupling signals, which turns the slave system into an It\^o diffusion and prevents exact synchronization. Comparing the stochastic synchronization error with the deterministic reference error obtained from noiseless observations, we show that bounded master and reference paths and sufficiently strong scalar coupling yield an $\mathcal O(\sigma^2)$ mean-square bound on their deviation, together with a tail-probability estimate; the bound becomes time-uniform when the deterministic slave field and its spatial derivative can be bounded uniformly in time. Both results use a Fourier-space norm induced by the physical-space $L^2$-norm, so Parseval's identity transfers the spectral bounds directly to the physical fields. Under additional regularity assumptions on the smoothness of the deterministic master and slave fields, we also obtain a mean-square bound on the stochastic synchronization error with respect to the infinite-dimensional (non-truncated) master system. These analytical results are illustrated by the numerical simulation of two master--slave systems, built around the Kawahara and Nikolaevskiy equations.
item.dc:creator: Joaqu\'in Miguez, In\'es P. Mari\~no

item.title: Integrable multi-species SSEP with reactive particle species
item.description: arXiv:2607.18959v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate integrable exclusion Markov processes constructed from set-theoretical solutions of the Yang-Baxter Equation (YBE) that generalise the multi-species Symmetric Simple Exclusion Process (SSEP). We first introduce the process called the $ (p,1) $-SSEP that is analogous to the multi-species SSEP but with an extra particle species qualified as reactive. Reactive species are able to evaporate and condense by pairs or to transform by pairs depending on the interpretation. We provide a full combinatorial study of the sectors in the periodic case. We prove the integrability of the process in the periodic case and in the open case for two types of boundaries that we introduce using Baxterisations of solutions of the reflection equation. Next we move on to the process called $ (p,q) $-SSEP, i.e. the multi-species SSEP with an arbitrary number of reactive particle species. We prove its integrability in the periodic case and, for the open case, we introduce integrable boundaries generalising the ones considered for the $ (p,1) $-SSEP. Finally, we define physical quantities relevant to the models and we compute them in the non-equilibrium stationary state of the open $ (p,q) $-SSEP for one type of integrable boundaries.
item.dc:creator: Mathieu Dabrowski, Lo\"ic Poulain d'Andecy, Eric Ragoucy

item.title: Odd elasticity in a three-link microswimmer: feedback equivalence, global controllability, and the cost of non-reciprocity
item.description: arXiv:2608.02777v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a Purcell three-link microswimmer whose joints are \emph{odd-elastic}: the torsional stiffness is non-Hermitian, its antisymmetric part $k_o$ injecting mechanical work so that the internal elastic drift is non-conservative. Our main finding is a sharp separation between geometry and cost --- odd elasticity is invisible to the control geometry of the swimmer and visible only in the energy of a manoeuvre. The mechanism is a single algebraic fact: the drift lies in the span of the two control vector fields, so the system is feedback-equivalent to a driftless one and the odd modulus enters the bracket structure only through the scalar $\det\textbf{K}=k^2+k_o^2$. From this we deduce that the abnormal extremals of the energy problem are unchanged by $k_o$, that the swimmer is globally controllable for every non-reciprocity with no threshold, and that its nilpotent model is the Cartan $(2,3,5)$ sub-Riemannian structure, deformed only by the metric scaling $g_\chi=(1+\chi^2)g_0$. The odd modulus acts solely on the cost: casting the optimal-steering problem in sub-Finsler (Randers) form, we prove that a prescribed reorientation is strictly cheaper for either sign of $k_o$. Full Resistive-Force-Theory simulations confirm the analysis and reveal that at isotropic drag the swimmer becomes a pure rotator, turning without translating.
item.dc:creator: Rossella Attanasi, Gaetano Napoli, Marta Zoppello

item.title: The equivalence of topological indices for $\mathrm{U}(1)\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetric quantum spin chains
item.description: arXiv:2609.34119v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases in quantum spin chains are distinguished by topological indices. Ogata's operator-algebraic indices apply to a broad range of symmetry classes without requiring continuous symmetry, whereas the elementary twist index of Tasaki requires $\mathrm{U}(1)$ symmetry. We prove their equivalence in the common setting of integer-spin chains with on-site $\mathrm{U}(1)\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry and a symmetric locally-unique gapped ground state, without assuming translation invariance or a matrix product representation. A charge-fluctuation estimate yields a strong-limit construction of half-chain rotations with their phases fixed. An exact group commutator identity then identifies the Ogata index with the limit of local twist expectations and gives an explicit error bound. This provides a computable formula for the index when a lower bound on the gap and the relevant ground-state expectations are available. Combining the equivalence with a recent boundary-field gap theorem of OpenAI and our earlier twist-index calculation, we obtain a spin-rotation-invariant locally-unique gapped ground state of the infinite $S=1$ antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chain with both indices equal to $-1$, without assuming infinite-volume uniqueness. The author formulated the problem and proposed the basic strategy, while ChatGPT Astra made substantial contributions to the development of the proof.
item.dc:creator: Hal Tasaki

item.title: On the signaling dimension of the cross-polytope
item.description: arXiv:2610.05924v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the general probabilistic model of information theory, the signaling dimension of a given communication protocol (or, equivalently, of its state space) is the smallest possible complexity of a classical communication protocol capable of perfectly simulating the given one in terms of input-output correlations. The signaling dimensions of three-, four-, and five-dimensional cross-polytopes have been known to be 3. We give logarithmic lower and upper bounds for the signaling dimensions of higher dimensional cross-polytopes, pinning down the value up to an additive gap of 2. The lower bound shows that the signaling dimension goes to infinity, in contrast to the case of balls and hypercubes.
item.dc:creator: Tam\'as Bencze, P\'eter E. Frenkel

item.title: Nematic order in monomer-dimer models of Heilmann and Lieb with lateral attraction in dimensions $d\ge 2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.08600v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the $d$-dimensional generalization of Models II ($d=2$) and V ($d=3$) for liquid crystals introduced by Heilmann--Lieb (1979), which consists of dimers on the hypercubic lattice at chemical potential $\mu$, interacting via a hard-core repulsion and a lateral attraction between parallel dimers with coupling constant $b>0$. For $d\in\{2,3\}$, these models were conjectured to exhibit liquid-crystalline order at low temperatures provided that $\mu+2(d-1)b>0$. We establish nematic order for all $d\ge 2$ under the additional condition $(4d-6)b>\mu$, which corresponds to the physical regime in which misaligned dimers are rare on scales comparable to the correlation length of the one-dimensional reference system. While the treatment of orientational order here follows the approach of our recent work on Model I, the proof of the absence of translational order relies on a custom implementation of cluster swapping in the sense of Sheffield (2005). Consequently, we deduce uniqueness of Gibbs measure and anisotropic exponential decay of correlations within each oriented phase.
item.dc:creator: Qidong He

item.title: A proof of Saari's homographic conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2212.10148v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove Saari's homographic conjecture for a large class of $n$-body problems with power law potentials, including the classical $n$-body problem.
item.dc:creator: Pieter Tibboel

item.title: Rational Q-systems at Root of Unity I. Closed Chains
item.description: arXiv:2310.14966v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The solution of Bethe ansatz equations for XXZ spin chain with the parameter $q$ being a root of unity is infamously subtle. In this work, we develop the rational $Q$-system for this case, which offers a systematic way to find all physical solutions of the Bethe ansatz equations at root of unity. The construction contains two parts. In the first part, we impose additional constraints to the rational $Q$-system. These constraints eliminate the so-called Fabricius-McCoy (FM) string solutions, yielding all primitive solutions. In the second part, we give a simple procedure to construct the descendant tower of any given primitive state. The primitive solutions together with their descendant towers constitute the complete Hilbert space. We test our proposal by extensive numerical checks and apply it to compute the torus partition function of the 6-vertex model at root of unity.
item.dc:creator: Jue Hou, Yunfeng Jiang, Yuan Miao

item.title: Limit theorems for the number of sign and level-set clusters of the Gaussian free field
item.description: arXiv:2501.14707v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the limiting fluctuations of the number of sign and level-set clusters of the Gaussian free field on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d \ge 3$, that are contained in a large domain. In dimension $d \ge 4$ we prove that the fluctuations are Gaussian at all non-critical levels, while in dimension $d=3$ we show that fluctuations may be Gaussian or non-Gaussian depending on the level. We also show that the sign clusters experience a form of Berry cancellation in all dimensions, that is, the fluctuations of the sign cluster count are suppressed compared to generic levels. Our proof is based on controlling the Wiener-It\^{o} chaos expansion of the cluster count using percolation theoretic inputs; to our knowledge this is the first time that chaos expansion techniques have been applied to analyse a non-local functional of a strongly correlated Gaussian field.
item.dc:creator: Michael McAuley, Stephen Muirhead

item.title: Fusion rules and structure constants of E-series minimal models
item.description: arXiv:2502.14295v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In the ADE classification of Virasoro minimal models, the E-series is the sparsest: their central charges $c=1-6\frac{(p-q)^2}{pq}$ are not dense in the half-line $c\in (-\infty,1)$, due to $q=12,18,30$ taking only 3 values -- the Coxeter numbers of $E_6, E_7, E_8$. The E-series is also the least well understood, with few known results beyond the spectrum. Here, we use a semi-analytic bootstrap approach for numerically computing 4-point correlation functions. We deduce non-chiral fusion rules, i.e. which 3-point structure constants vanish. These vanishings can be explained by constraints from null vectors, interchiral symmetry, simple currents, extended symmetries, permutations, and parity, except in one case for $q=30$. We conjecture that structure constants are given by a universal expression built from the double Gamma function, times polynomial functions of $\cos(\pi\frac{p}{q})$ with values in $\mathbb{Q}\big(\cos(\frac{\pi}{q})\big)$, which we work out explicitly for $q=12$. We speculate on generalizing E-series minimal models to generic integer values of $q$, and recovering loop CFTs as $p,q\to \infty$.
item.dc:creator: Rongvoram Nivesvivat, Sylvain Ribault

item.title: Symmetry defects and gauging for quantum states with matrix product unitary symmetries
item.description: arXiv:2502.20257v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we examine the consequences of the existence of a finite group of matrix product unitary (MPU) symmetries for matrix product states (MPS). We generalize the well-understood picture of onsite unitary symmetries, which give rise to virtual symmetry defects given by insertions of operators in the bonds of the MPS. In the MPU case, we can define analogous defect tensors, this time sitting on lattice sites, that can be created, moved, and fused by local unitary operators. We leverage this formalism to study the gauging of MPU symmetries. We introduce a condition, block independence, under which we can gauge the symmetries by promoting the symmetry defects to gauge degrees of freedom, yielding an MPS of the same bond dimension that supports a local version of the symmetry given by commuting gauge constraints. Whenever block independence does not hold (which happens, in particular, whenever the symmetry representation is anomalous), a modification of our method which we call state-level gauging still gives rise to a locally symmetric MPS by promotion of the symmetry defects, at the expense of producing gauge constraints that do not commute on different sites.
item.dc:creator: Adri\'an Franco-Rubio, Arkadiusz Bochniak, J. Ignacio Cirac

item.title: Existence and Smoothing for a Nondivergence-Form Degenerate Diffusion from Plasma-Wave Theory
item.description: arXiv:2503.13922v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove existence, positive-time smoothing, and physical admissibility of weak solutions to the degenerate parabolic Cauchy-Dirichlet problem $\partial_t u = \rho_\lambda(x) u \partial_x^2 u + \rho_\lambda(x) g(x) u$ on the half-line, where $\rho_\lambda$ vanishes at the boundary and grows at infinity. This scalar problem arises by formally reducing the system of equations given by the quasilinear theory of plasma waves in the one-dimensional case. This theory models a background distribution of electrons $f$ coupled to a spectral energy density $W$ through wave-particle resonance. For the scalar problem we construct weak solutions from weighted $L^p$ initial data and bounded reaction, admitting the unbounded, discontinuous data that the physical model demands, and lying beyond the reach of the continuous-data theories developed for nearby problems. We identify a parabolic smoothing effect for the constructed solution, namely one-sided bounds on $\partial_t u$: from merely integrable data, the solution becomes locally H\"older in space and time and locally Lipschitz in space at positive times. This spatial regularity is shown to be sharp by explicit examples. Finally, we address the quasilinear system itself, whose well-posedness remains open: we prove that the scalar solution induces a particle-wave pair $(f^{\ast}, W^{\ast})$ which is a weak solution of the system. Under nonnegativity and finite-moment hypotheses on the initial data, both components remain nonnegative and the initial mass is conserved. Moreover, the pair inherits positive-time regularity, with $W^{\ast}$ decaying quantitatively at large wavenumber and $f^{\ast}$ smoothing to a locally bounded function even when initially a measure.
item.dc:creator: William Porteous, Irene M. Gamba, Kun Huang

item.title: A Constructive Definition of Space via Dynamical Evolution and Observational Acts
item.description: arXiv:2505.09838v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose a constructive and dynamical redefinition of spatial structure, grounded in the interplay between mechanical evolution and observational acts. Rather than presupposing space as a static background, we interpret space as an emergent entity that arises through observational acts. Given a time evolution and a physically specified measurement context, we construct a reachability structure and a context-dependent measurable structure. Using the framework of pre-topologies, measurable structures, and the GNS construction, we analyze how the choice of observables and the system's time evolution dynamically determine the topological and measure-theoretic features of space. Time evolution and the measurement context are inputs to this construction. Deriving time itself or a complete dynamics for the selection and stabilization of the measurement context lies outside the scope of this paper. This approach highlights the observer-dependent and context-sensitive nature of spatial concepts in both classical and quantum domains.
item.dc:creator: So Katagiri

item.title: Conifold gap and all-genus mirror symmetry for local $\mathbb{P}^2$
item.description: arXiv:2509.19298v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Conifold Gap Conjecture asserts that the polar part of the Gromov-Witten potential of a Calabi-Yau threefold near its conifold locus has a universal expression described by the logarithm of the Barnes $G$-function. In this paper, I prove the Conifold Gap Conjecture for the local projective plane.
